item.description: Loss-making and deeply indebted US cloud company CoreWeave became an easy target this week for investors concerned about an artificial intelligence bubble. Its selloff, though, has greater significance for markets than its size implies.
item.dc:creator: Vidya Ranganathan, Aditya Soni
item.content:encoded: Loss-making and deeply indebted US [USN:L4N46111C TEXT:"cloud company CoreWeave"] (CRWV.O) became an easy target this week for investors concerned about an artificial intelligence bubble. Its selloff, though, has greater significance for markets than its size implies. The [USN:L4N461177 TEXT:"slump"] in the shares and bonds of the $39 billion Nvidia-backed (NVDA.O) AI infrastructure company came after third-quarter reports from hyperscalers hinted at delays in data center projects and a slower pace of growth in capital expenditure. Worried investors took aim at new-age AI-based cloud firms, or neoclouds, such as CoreWeave, conceivably the weakest links in [USN:L4N461177 TEXT:"the AI ecosystem"] because of how they borrow heavily to finance chips, land and energy for data centers which will yield income only in the future. CoreWeave's shares dived more than 15% this week while yields on its 2030 bonds jumped 500 basis points to near 16%. CoreWeave chief Mike Intrator told employees in a [USN:L4N4601XL TEXT:"memo"], seen by Reuters, markets can sometimes "misunderstand and act irrationally" and it has a strong pipeline of demand. The company did not respond to Reuters' requests for comment. Investors focused instead on its $50 billion debt and the perils of being trapped in the middle of a [USN:L4N461177 TEXT:"circular"] financing arrangement between chipmakers such as Nvidia and clients such as Meta Platforms (META.O) and OpenAI. "The problem with this stuff is that we're talking about huge interconnectedness, not just circular financing but the fact that these assets are all held in the same places, in the same portfolios, by the same types of investors," said James Athey, fixed-income portfolio manager at Marlborough. "And leverage is always that thing which turns a storm into a teacup into something more nefarious," he said, referring broadly to the AI jitters. Companies such as CoreWeave, Nebius (NBIS.O) , Applied Digital (APLD.O) , Iren (IREN.O) , Lambda Labs, Crusoe and TeraWulf (WULF.O) are building energy-intensive data centers they can eventually rent out to firms developing and running AI models. That calls for massive upfront investment and very little income until the leases begin. CoreWeave has never turned a profit, according to data compiled by LSEG. CoreWeave's CEO also said in the memo that [USN:L4N4601XL TEXT:"its deal backlog"] more than covers its [USN:L4N461177 TEXT:"debt"] obligations. The company had a $104.2 billion revenue backlog at the end of the second quarter, followed by [USN:L6N4590TM TEXT:"more than $25 billion"] in new commitments early in the third quarter. But the New Jersey-based company is burning cash faster than investors like. In 2025, CoreWeave reported annual revenue of $5.1 billion and a net loss of $1.2 billion. While revenue is expected to double this year, capital expenditure is estimated to be up fourfold to between $35 billion and $39 billion, leading to even more cash burn this year. News that Intrator and entities linked to him have [USN:L6N4620WG TEXT:"sold nearly $1 billion of stock"] since the company's IPO in March last year, mostly under prearranged trading plans as per regulatory filings, has not helped. "Clearly they will need a capital injection or a bailout. They are burning capital, and capital is no longer free," said Alberto Gallo, founder of hedge fund Andromeda Capital. "You want to buy debt in businesses that have visible cash flow, typically as a bond investor, not someone that is doing capex, in the hope that there will be more capex needed in the future," he said. The firm holds bets against CoreWeave bonds. DOUBTS APLENTY CoreWeave is at the top of the 100-odd [USN:L6N46113P TEXT:"neoclouds"] that research firm Gartner Inc says are "the most exposed to the imbalance between revenue and capital spending" and need to soon earn returns to sustain operations. Gartner expects that by 2030, 80% of neocloud providers will cease independent operations. "We are in a situation in which there are a lot of expectations on revenues and revenue growth, but this revenue growth is being fueled by the wrong type of capital, which is debt, not equity," said Tommaso Leodari, Dubai-based chief investment officer of hedge fund Index & Cie. The fund does not hold stakes in pure AI firms. "In the specific case of CoreWeave, these guys are financing their entire business with debt. So if anything happens in the utilization of this particular asset or if there is a slowing down on the construction of these data centers, it will reflect in problems in repaying the debt." A streak of warnings from AI hyperscalers such as Microsoft (MSFT.O) and [USN:L4N45G12J TEXT:"Oracle"] Corp (ORCL.N) on delays in data center projects, power and component bottlenecks, a glut in high-end chips, alongside plans by giants such as Meta and Microsoft to launch their own chips to rival Nvidia's, have also stoked concerns about neoclouds. The pace at which revenue is growing at AI giants such as OpenAI and Anthropic, while still fast, has also softened. "Even at $10 billion revenue, CoreWeave is losing $2.5 billion, so there are no scale effects in the industry clear as yet," wrote Michael Frazis of Sydney-based Frazis Capital Partners. CoreWeave has Nvidia's backing. The chip giant has agreed to buy unsold CoreWeave compute capacity through April 2032, [USN:L3N3V20QW TEXT:"guaranteeing"] it will have a buyer for capacity not sold to customers. Ratings agencies have CoreWeave's debt marked as speculative grade, yet Sean Cray, vice president at Moody’s Ratings, pointed out the company does not speculatively purchase chips and has multiple avenues for financing. Originally a bitcoin miner, CoreWeave has still been an easy mark for punters, and hedge funds have been buying its junk-rated bonds for the high yield. The [USN:L6N4610J0 TEXT:"cost of insuring its debt"] against default climbed to about 1,200 basis points this week, signalling severe distress. "CoreWeave's credit selloff risks becoming a self-fulfilling prophecy," wrote Saurav Sen at research firm Gimme Credit. "The concern is less whether customers want the capacity than whether CoreWeave can afford to deliver it."

item.title: Bucks move start time for home opener, avoid World Series conflict
item.description: The NBA moved up the tipoff of the Bucks' home opener against the Chicago Bulls on Oct. 23 to avoid a conflict with Game 1 of the World Series, which will be held in Milwaukee that evening.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The NBA moved up the tipoff of the Bucks' home opener against the Chicago Bulls on Oct. 23 to avoid a conflict with Game 1 of the World Series, which will be held in Milwaukee that evening. Per the Bucks, their home opener was moved to 3 p.m. CT. The original start time for the game was 7 p.m., the same as the first pitch of Game 1 of the Fall Classic. The Milwaukee Brewers punched their ticket to the World Series on Thursday by completing a four-game sweep of the Los Angeles Dodgers in the National League Championship Series. The Brewers will face either the Tampa Bay Rays or Cleveland Guardians. The Guardians lead 2-1 in the American League best-of-seven series. "The Brewers' return to the World Series for the first time in 44 years is a special moment for Milwaukee and sports fans across Wisconsin," the Bucks said in a statement. "Congratulations to the Brewers and the entire organization on this tremendous achievement, and we'll be cheering them on as they begin their World Series run." --Field Level Media

item.title: Irish public sector trade unions suspend second day of strikes
item.description: Irish public sector trade unions suspended a second day of widespread strikes planned for next week after they agreed on Friday to begin mediated discussions with the government this weekend on the terms for new pay talks.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Irish public sector trade unions suspended a second day of widespread strikes planned for next week after they agreed on Friday to begin mediated discussions with the government this weekend on the terms for new pay talks. Much of Ireland's public sector including teachers, health workers and civil servants on Wednesday staged the country's [USN:L1N4600B0 TEXT:"first major strike"] in almost two decades after failing for months to agree with ministers on the basis for negotiations on pay rises. The two sides agreed on Friday to begin a process aimed at finding a basis for formal negotiations to commence. "I believe that there is now a prospect of progress in the process that has been established. Obviously we will need to see the government's words backed up in practice," Kevin Callinan, chair of the Irish Congress of Trade Unions public services committee, told national broadcaster RTE.

item.title: Novartis ends mid-stage Fabhalta trial targeting serious kidney condition
item.description: Swiss drugmaker Novartis has terminated a mid-stage study testing its drug Fabhalta in patients with a serious kidney condition, citing "strategic considerations", according to a federal clinical trials registry.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Swiss drugmaker Novartis (NOVN.S) has terminated a mid-stage study testing its drug Fabhalta in patients with a serious kidney condition, citing "strategic considerations", according to a federal clinical trials registry. The trial was evaluating whether the oral medication was safe and effective for treating lupus nephritis when added to standard medical care Lupus nephritis is a severe inflammation of the kidneys caused by the autoimmune disease lupus The government database, last updated on October 15, shows Novartis decided to conclude the study after completing the first part It gives no other explanation and does not say whether safety or effectiveness played a role Endpoints News reported the development earlier on Friday Novartis did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment The US FDA first approved Fabhalta in 2023 for a rare blood disorder called PNH. It has since been approved for two kidney diseases, IgA nephropathy and C3 glomerulopathy

item.title: Enviado de Putin diz que Rússia e EUA discutem acordos conjuntos, incluindo data centres
item.description: Rússia e EUA estão discutindo uma série de novos projetos conjuntos, incluindo data centres movidos a energia nuclear, na esteira do acordo sobre diesel firmado na semana passada, disse nesta sexta-feira o enviado para investimentos do presidente Vladimir Putin.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Soldatkin, Olesya Astakhova
item.content:encoded: Rússia e EUA estão discutindo uma série de novos projetos conjuntos, incluindo data centres movidos a energia nuclear, na esteira do acordo sobre diesel firmado na semana passada, disse nesta sexta-feira o enviado para investimentos do presidente Vladimir Putin. Kirill Dmitriev afirmou que as sanções dos EUA representam sérios obstáculos e criticou como “equivocada” a Lei Graham, assinada pelo presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, no mês passado, que visa reduzir as receitas energéticas da Rússia por meio de sanções e tarifas. No entanto, ele disse que os dois países estão considerando outras formas de cooperação econômica na esteira do acordo sobre o diesel. “Também estamos discutindo projetos conjuntos na área de data centres russos e norte-americanos, inclusive com o uso de usinas nucleares de pequena escala”, acrescentou ele, sem dar detalhes. Neste mês, a Ucrânia atacou centros de dados do grupo de tecnologia russo Yandex e do grupo bancário e tecnológico Sberbank, no que classificou como uma resposta a ataques russos contra instalações ucranianas. Dmitriev, figura-chave nas negociações entre a Rússia e os EUA para pôr fim à guerra na Ucrânia, vem há muito tempo pressionando por uma série de acordos potenciais ambiciosos, inclusive sobre minerais e energia. O Kremlin tem manifestado frustração pelo fato de os EUA, até agora, terem vinculado tais acordos a um acordo de paz, que continua indefinido. Mas Dmitriev demonstrou otimismo de que isso está mudando. “Naturalmente, o progresso é bastante difícil; há resistência — resistência generalizada, na verdade — de vários setores. No entanto, como demonstra o exemplo do diesel, acredito que em breve anunciaremos várias outras iniciativas significativas. O gelo, de fato, começou a se quebrar”, disse ele na conferência Russian Energy Week, em Moscou. “Estamos efetivamente implementando projetos com os Estados Unidos da América neste exato momento e continuaremos a fazê-lo até que a operação militar especial chegue ao fim”, acrescentou ele, usando o termo do Kremlin para se referir à guerra. Dmitriev disse que o Tesouro dos EUA havia solicitado ao fundo soberano da Rússia, que ele dirige, que ajudasse a resolver questões complexas de pagamento relacionadas ao acordo sobre o diesel. O acordo anunciado por Trump há uma semana envolve o fornecimento de diesel russo aos mercados dos EUA e globais, a fim de reduzir o preço do combustível — uma prioridade para o presidente dos EUA antes das eleições de meio de mandato do próximo mês.

item.title: Swiss finance minister warns steep European debt could trigger euro crisis
item.description: Rising public debt levels in Europe and beyond pose a risk to economic stability and could trigger a euro crisis, Swiss Finance Minister Karin Keller-Sutter said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Rising public debt levels in Europe and beyond pose a risk to economic stability and could trigger a euro crisis, Swiss Finance Minister Karin Keller-Sutter said on Friday. Speaking to Swiss national broadcaster SRF in Bangkok on the sidelines of the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, Keller-Sutter said energy prices were also fuelling concerns among policymakers. Switzerland has one of the lowest levels of public debt in Europe, but Keller-Sutter said it was important to see the bigger picture in the current environment. "We're so deeply interconnected internationally that we're also vulnerable, for instance, in case a debt crisis arises due to the sovereign debt of major countries. "I'm thinking in particular of the United States, but also of Europe; we have France - that could lead to a euro crisis," Keller-Sutter told SRF. France's public debt, budget deficits and tepid economic growth have [USN:L6N45Y0KA TEXT:"fed concern"] about its finances as political fragmentation has complicated fiscal consolidation efforts.

item.title: Trump says neither he nor Musk responsible for Ukraine loss of Starlink access
item.description: US President Donald Trump said on Friday that he did not think either he or Elon Musk was responsible for Ukraine losing Starlink access in a way that affected its military operations against Russia.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump said on Friday that he did not think either he or Elon Musk was responsible for Ukraine losing Starlink access in a way that affected its military operations against Russia. The reduction in services provided by the satellite company interrupted communications with headquarters and caused internet speeds to drop. Reuters reported on Thursday that the White House approved the [USN:L1N4610ZC TEXT:"reduction in Starshield services"]. Trump, speaking to reporters as he left the White House on a trip to Georgia, said neither he nor Musk was responsible for Ukraine losing Starlink access. Any limit to Ukraine's access to the Starshield system was not imposed by the United States, Trump added. Starshield was developed by SpaceX specifically for government and national-security customers, particularly the US Department of Defense. Starshield uses the Starlink constellation as its backbone. Trump also he has a good relationship with Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskiy.

item.title: Division II DB Tyler Ulrich dies days after in-game injury
item.description: A North Texas community and an Oklahoma college campus are in mourning following the death of defensive back Tyler Ulrich, who died five days after suffering a traumatic injury in a game.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A North Texas community and an Oklahoma college campus are in mourning following the death of defensive back Tyler Ulrich, who died five days after suffering a traumatic injury in a game. Ulrich, from Azle, Texas, was injured in the game between his team, Southern Nazarene, and Ouachita Baptist in Arkadelphia, Ark., last Saturday in an NCAA Division II meeting. The school announced the passing of the sophomore finance major on Thursday. "When I think of good, I think of Tyler Ulrich," Jason Vines, who coached him at Azle High School, told WFAA. "One of the sweetest young men I've ever been around, ever known." Southern Nazarene, based in Bethany, Okla., canceled its game set for this Saturday at Southwestern Oklahoma State. After the 49-14 loss at Ouachita, the university confirmed Ulrich, 21, was in critical condition but never specified the injury. In a statement issued Thursday, Southern Nazarene asked the community to keep Ulrich's family in their thoughts. "This loss is deeply felt across our campus," read a school statement posted to X. "Our hearts are with his family, friends, teammates, and everyone who knew him. We ask that you join us in lifting them up in prayer." In six games for Southern Nazarene this season, Ulrich made 39 tackles. He was in his third season with the Crimson Storm. --Field Level Media

item.title: Djokovic returns to Basel for first time since 2011 in ATP Finals bid
item.description: Novak Djokovic on Friday received a wildcard entry into the Swiss Indoors Basel, setting up his first appearance at the tournament since 2011 as the 24-times Grand Slam champion pursues a place at the ATP Finals and the 103rd title of his career.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Novak Djokovic on Friday received a wildcard entry into the Swiss Indoors Basel, setting up his first appearance at the tournament since 2011 as the 24-times Grand Slam champion pursues a place at the ATP Finals and the 103rd title of his career. The 39-year-old Serbian arrives in Switzerland after a mixed Asian swing, where he captured a [USN:L6N45S0UI TEXT:"record seventh China Open crown"] before suffering a [USN:L1N45V0DT TEXT:"surprise second-round defeat"] by Poland's Hubert Hurkacz at the Shanghai Masters, a tournament he has won a record four times. Djokovic has endured an uneven season by his lofty standards. The former world number one [USN:L4N44R04U TEXT:"exited the US Open"] in the first round, his earliest Grand Slam defeat since the 2006 Australian Open. The decision to add Basel to his schedule comes as something of a surprise after Djokovic said following his early exit in Shanghai that he planned to play only the Paris Masters, scheduled for November 2-8, before the season-ending ATP Finals. Basel offers Djokovic an opportunity to strengthen his bid for a 17th ATP Finals appearance. He sits 11th in the ATP Live Race to Turin and needs to finish inside the top nine, with world number one [USN:L1N45S0CV TEXT:"Jannik Sinner sidelined"] for the remainder of 2026 because of a persistent knee injury. Djokovic will make his fourth appearance in Basel, having lifted the trophy in 2009 by beating Swiss great Roger Federer in the final. He joins a strong field that includes Canadian Felix Auger-Aliassime and Americans Ben Shelton and Taylor Fritz at the ATP 500 indoor hardcourt event, which runs from October 26-November 1.

item.title: White House press secretary Zacharia fired in less than a week after facing criticism
item.description: The move comes after Trump said he had told her to reconsider the job following public scrutiny. Trump had described Zacharia as an attorney when he announced her appointment. During a Fox News interview, Zacharia said she did not pass the bar.
item.dc:creator: Nandita Bose, Trevor Hunnicutt, Jasper Ward
item.content:encoded: White House press secretary [USN:FWN45V14O TEXT:"Katie Zacharia"] was fired after less than a week on the job, two US officials said on Friday, after a rocky start as President Donald Trump 's top spokesperson. Zacharia was "let go" and is "transitioning out" of the press secretary position, according to two separate White House officials. She faced days of questions about her [USN:L6N4601D0 TEXT:"legal credentials"] and criticism of her performance in a news briefing and interviews. The departure leaves Trump without a key public messenger just over two weeks before November's midterm elections , a critical period when the president is seeking to tout his administration's accomplishments and help his fellow Republicans retain control of Congress. Trump told reporters earlier on Friday that he had asked Zacharia to reconsider whether to continue in her role after facing tough press coverage during her first days on the job. "I told her: 'I think you're better off being happy, and I'm not sure you can ever be happy in this stuff.' There's nothing easy about this stuff," Trump told reporters as he departed the White House for a weekend trip. He added: "I said to her honestly, 'If I were you, I'd reconsider... think about it. But I would reconsider.'" Trump said he intended to revisit the conversation with Zacharia later. Zacharia started on Monday and held her debut White House briefing on Tuesday. She said she received a call about the press secretary role on October 7 and was offered the job to succeed [USN:FWN4491F6 TEXT:"Karoline Leavitt"] a week ago. She soon faced questions about her career, which she said included a tenure practicing law. Trump had also described her as an attorney. "I practiced international transaction law, with all the appropriate credentials," Zacharia said in an emailed statement on Wednesday. Reuters could not find records showing the Pepperdine University law school graduate was registered as an attorney or member of the bar in any US state or the District of Columbia. During a Fox News interview on Thursday, Zacharia said she [USN:L1N46201S TEXT:"did not pass the bar"] exam. Law school graduates cannot legally practice law in the US without first being admitted to a state bar. Zacharia and the White House did not immediately respond to an email seeking comment about her firing. Earlier on Friday, she told reporters at the White House that she was looking forward to working with the press. Trump hired Zacharia after expressing concerns about the media coverage of his administration, feeling he needed a new spokesperson who could amplify his achievements, according to two people familiar with the conversations. In a phone interview with Fox on Friday, Trump said he was in no rush to name a new press secretary. Zacharia's quick exit meant she had what is believed to be the shortest tenure of any press secretary in the role's history. "Records are made to be broken," Anthony Scaramucci, who served as director of communications for 10 days during Trump's first administration, said on X. "But I take no pleasure in other people's pain."

item.title: Sheinbaum y Bukele no discutieron públicamente sobre sus sistemas educativos
item.description: La presidenta de México, Claudia Sheinbaum, y el presidente de El Salvador, Nayib Bukele, no discutieron públicamente sobre sus sistemas educativos, contrario a lo que sugieren publicaciones con un video alterado de la mandataria mexicana y un discurso de su homólogo salvadoreño en el que no menciona a México.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: La presidenta de México, Claudia Sheinbaum, y el presidente de El Salvador, Nayib Bukele, no discutieron públicamente sobre sus sistemas educativos, contrario a lo que sugieren publicaciones con un video alterado de la mandataria mexicana y un discurso de su homólogo salvadoreño en el que no menciona a México. Ejemplos en internet dicen que, después de que Bukele anunció en agosto la entrega de 50 mil becas, Sheinbaum declaró en una conferencia que él solo busca un "espectáculo". Según las publicaciones, el presidente salvadoreño le respondió en un evento. Sin embargo, no hay evidencia de que la presidenta hiciera el comentario que se le atribuye. Las imágenes del primer fragmento corresponden a una conferencia de prensa matutina del 24 de agosto y, de acuerdo con el video completo y la versión estenográfica , no hizo referencia a Bukele o a sus iniciativas. No se identificaron declaraciones similares de Sheinbaum en medios de comunicación y en sus cuentas de redes sociales oficiales . El equipo de Comunicación Social de Presidencia de México dijo a Reuters el 13 de octubre en un mensaje de WhatsApp que el contenido es falso. El presidente salvadoreño publicó el segundo fragmento del video en su canal de YouTube el 15 de septiembre. En él, pidió a la ministra de Educación avanzar en mejoras educativas y habló sobre las becas para estudios superiores, no hizo referencia al modelo educativo mexicano o Sheinbaum. La presidencia de El Salvador no respondió inmediatamente a una solicitud de comentarios. Reuters ha abordado otras publicaciones que adjudican comentarios sin sustento a los políticos. VEREDICTO Falso. La presidenta de México, Claudia Sheinbaum, no criticó el programa de becas de Nayib Bukele y su homólogo salvadoreño no respondió a esos cuestionamientos. Reuters Fact Check ofrece información confiable mediante su canal de WhatsApp para México . Envíenos un mensaje con el contenido en español que desea que verifiquemos. Este artículo fue realizado por el equipo de Reuters Fact Check. Lea más sobre nuestro trabajo de verificación de afirmaciones en las redes sociales.

item.title: Real Madrid pede saída do presidente da LaLiga após comparação com propaganda nazista
item.description: O Real Madrid pediu nesta sexta-feira a renúncia do presidente da LaLiga, Javier Tebas, depois que ele comparou a retórica da diretoria do clube aos métodos de propaganda utilizados pelo Partido Nazista na Alemanha.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O Real Madrid pediu nesta sexta-feira a renúncia do presidente da LaLiga, Javier Tebas, depois que ele comparou a retórica da diretoria do clube aos métodos de propaganda utilizados pelo Partido Nazista na Alemanha. Tebas escreveu na manhã desta sexta-feira nas redes sociais que “a diretoria do Real Madrid conduz uma orquestra de porta-vozes e a Real Madrid TV lidera o coro”. O presidente da LaLiga estava respondendo a artigos de dois jornalistas que afirmavam que ele e a LaLiga estavam agindo contra os interesses do Real. Tebas acrescentou que os autores no jornal El Debate estavam amplificando uma mensagem em nome da diretoria do Real Madrid. A Reuters solicitou um comentário ao El Debate. A demanda do Real Madrid para que Tebas saia imediatamente aprofunda a disputa entre o clube e o presidente da LaLiga. Em setembro, o Real pediu a nomeação de um novo presidente da LaLiga em resposta a Tebas, que classificou as reclamações do clube sobre as decisões de arbitragem como “uma cortina de fumaça” para encobrir suas deficiências em campo. Tebas criticou, na sexta-feira, a cobertura da Real Madrid TV sobre a arbitragem em suas partidas. “O roteiro deles é sempre o mesmo: selecionar as jogadas que lhes convêm, repetir as queixas, alimentar a desconfiança e apontar o dedo para os inimigos”, escreveu ele. “Esse método lembra os mecanismos de propaganda usados por Goebbels, ministro da Propaganda da Alemanha nazista." “A comparação é com essas técnicas de propaganda, não com uma ideologia ou, é claro, com a torcida madridista”, acrescentou o presidente da LaLiga. O Real Madrid divulgou um comunicado na sexta-feira pedindo que Tebas renuncie aos cargos de presidente da LaLiga e vice-presidente da Real Federação Espanhola de Futebol. O comunicado considerou “intolerável e extraordinariamente grave” o fato de Tebas ter usado “uma comparação com os métodos de propaganda do regime nazista para desacreditar nosso clube, sua diretoria e sua emissora de TV”. “A conduta repetida de Tebas demonstra falta de neutralidade, respeito e imparcialidade, incompatível com suas responsabilidades institucionais”, afirmou o Real. “É inaceitável que ele se aproveite até mesmo de perguntas, informações ou opiniões de jornalistas não ligados ao clube para direcionar suas acusações contra nós, atribuindo-nos ações de terceiros pelas quais não temos qualquer responsabilidade.” Tebas, de 64 anos, eleito pelos 42 clubes profissionais das duas principais divisões da Espanha, é presidente da LaLiga desde 2013. Em 2023, ele foi reeleito sem oposição até 2027.

item.title: Ações europeias fecham melhor semana desde junho com balanços amenizando impacto de vendas em tecnologia
item.description: As ações europeias subiram nesta sexta-feira, encerrando sua melhor semana desde o final de junho, com sólidos resultados financeiros ajudando a amenizar o impacto de uma onda global de vendas de ações do setor de tecnologia.
item.dc:creator: Avinash P, Niket Nishant
item.content:encoded: As ações europeias subiram nesta sexta-feira, encerrando sua melhor semana desde o final de junho, com sólidos resultados financeiros ajudando a amenizar o impacto de uma onda global de vendas de ações do setor de tecnologia. O índice pan-europeu STOXX 600 (.STOXX) subiu 0,7%, para 644,74 pontos, atingindo a maior cotação em mais de três semanas. O índice de referência acumulou alta de mais de 2% na semana. “Esta semana demonstrou o valor da diversificação quando o mercado tecnológico concentrado dos EUA fica sob pressão”, disse Daniela Hathorn, analista sênior de mercado da Capital.com. Uma onda de vendas em ações de empresas de tecnologia de grande destaque, motivada por preocupações com a crescente dependência de dívida para desenvolver infraestrutura de IA, aliada a receios quanto à concorrência da China, prejudicou as ações do setor de tecnologia nesta semana. No entanto, resultados sólidos da fabricante de equipamentos para chips de computador ASML (ASML.AS) , da fornecedora de sistemas de chips Aixtron (AIXGn.DE) e da fabricante de equipamentos de telecomunicações Ericsson (ERICb.ST) ajudaram a melhorar o ânimo do mercado. “Uma temporada de resultados financeiros muito positiva vai realmente impulsionar o ânimo dos investidores. Isso pode levar os mercados de volta a alguns dos picos que vimos recentemente”, disse Michael Field, estrategista-chefe de ações da Morningstar. Espera-se que os lucros das empresas do STOXX 600 aumentem 20,7% no terceiro trimestre em relação ao ano anterior, uma ligeira queda em relação à previsão de crescimento de 21% divulgada na semana passada, segundo dados da LSEG I/B/E/S. O índice pan-europeu STOXX 600 (.STOXX) fechou em alta de 0,67%, a 644,43 pontos. Em LONDRES, o índice Financial Times (.FTSE) avançou 0,38%, a 10.881,90 pontos. Em FRANKFURT, o índice DAX (.GDAXI) subiu 0,94%, a 25.622,42 pontos. Em PARIS, o índice CAC-40 (.FCHI) ganhou 0,28%, a 7.956,70 pontos. Em MILÃO, o índice Ftse/Mib (.FTMIB) teve valorização de 0,93%, a 49.857,18 pontos. Em MADRI, o índice Ibex-35 (.IBEX) registrou alta de 0,77%, a 19.326,30 pontos. Em LISBOA, o índice PSI20 (.PSI20) valorizou-se 1,01%, a 9.468,47 pontos.

item.title: Thames Water wins majority support among key Class B creditors for recapitalisation
item.description: Thames Water said on Friday it had reached an agreement with key Class B creditors on a proposed recapitalisation, securing support from holders of more than 60% of its junior Class B debt and advancing efforts to restructure Britain's biggest water utility.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Thames Water said on Friday it had reached an agreement with key Class B creditors on a proposed recapitalisation, securing support from holders of more than 60% of its junior Class B debt and advancing efforts to restructure Britain's biggest water utility. The proposal would see about £1 billion ($1.33 billion) of Class B debt written off, with those creditors receiving a roughly 5.9% recovery through equity and other rights in the restructured company in return. The deal marks progress for Thames Water's senior creditors, known as London & Valley Water consortium, who are pursuing a rescue plan involving debt writedowns and fresh equity investment to avert temporary government control of the utility. L&VW declined to comment. The utility, weighed down by about £20 billion in debt, is seeking to overhaul its debt-laden balance sheet through a broader recapitalisation as it works to improve its finances and services amid mounting fines for polluting rivers with sewage. On Thursday, Thames Water [USN:L8N4611UT TEXT:"said"] it needed to increase its emergency funding facility by £2.4 billion to £5.4 billion to avoid running out of cash before its planned recapitalisation is completed. Thames Water said talks with L&VW and regulators on the proposed recapitalisation were ongoing, with no decision yet taken on whether to proceed with the consortium's rescue plan. The future of Thames Water is being closely watched after Prime Minister Andy Burnham last month [USN:L8N45L19H TEXT:"pledged"] legislation allowing public ownership of water companies while the government and regulators consider the L&VW rescue plan for the utility. ($1 = 0.7511 pounds)

item.title: Police seek answers after children killed in Oregon school shooting
item.description: US police were investigating on Friday why a 16-year-old boy shot dead three children and a teacher at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon, and how he got hold of the long gun used in his attack.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US police were investigating on Friday why a 16-year-old boy shot dead three children and a teacher at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon, and how he got hold of the long gun used in his attack. The latest deadly school shooting in the United States [USN:L1N461173 TEXT:"unfolded on Thursday afternoon"] when the teenager, who has not been publicly identified, shot through a locked door at Silver Rail Elementary School in central Oregon, according to the Bend Police Department. The teenager killed three children aged 5, 8 and 11 and one teacher before he himself was shot dead by an armed bystander who had pursued him into the school, Police Chief Mike Krantz said at a Thursday evening press conference. Such shootings have become common in the US, with each one reviving debates over gun laws in a country where a right to "keep and bear Arms" is protected under the Constitution's Second Amendment. BYSTANDER INTERVENED The bystander has not been publicly identified by police, although the New York Times reported that he was the father of two young girls who attend the school. Oregon Governor Tina Kotek said at the press conference that the bystander "heroically intervened to stop further loss of life." Beyond those killed, a 7-year-old student and a 54-year-old teacher were taken to hospital with critical injuries. It was not clear if the shooter had any prior connection to the school, which has about 450 students from kindergarten through the fifth grade, roughly ages 5 to 11, and 40 staff members. The New York Times and other outlets, citing unnamed law enforcement officials, identified the teenager as John J. Griffin II, and investigators searched his home and seized electronic devices. They believe he used a 12-gauge pump-action Maverick 88 shotgun in the attack, which police say is registered to his mother, the Times reported. Officials at the Bend Police Department, who did not respond to questions on Friday, were due to give updates on their investigation at an afternoon press conference. GUN LAW DEBATES Some of the deadliest school attacks in the US include those at Columbine High School in 1999, Sandy Hook Elementary School in 2012, Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in 2018 and Robb Elementary School in Uvalde, Texas, in 2022. Advocates for gun-owners' rights have argued for arming teachers as a means of defense. The Gun Owners of America advocacy group pointed to the armed bystander's intervention in Bend as evidence for their position. Residents of the small city of Bend were left grieving after the attack, which unfolded in minutes, with emergency responders receiving a call at 12:59 p.m. PDT (1959 GMT) from a person in a vehicle who reported being shot at multiple times by someone with a long gun, police said. In the minutes afterwards, dozens of calls were received saying the shooter had entered the school. Officers arrived at 1:02 p.m. and moments later an officer reported the shooter had been killed, police said. Officers entered and confirmed the teenager was dead.

item.title: Stars sign David Perron, 38, to one-year contract
item.description: The Dallas Stars signed forward David Perron to a one-year, $850,000 contract on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Dallas Stars signed forward David Perron to a one-year, $850,000 contract on Friday. Perron, 38, will be playing in his 20th NHL season with his eighth team. He totaled 28 points (13 goals, 15 assists) in 65 games last season split with the Ottawa Senators and Detroit Red Wings. "We are excited to welcome David and his family to the Stars organization," general manager Jim Nill said. "He brings a competitive mindset and a proven ability to perform in big moments. We believe his veteran leadership and skill set will be a valuable addition to our group as we continue to build toward our goal of winning a Stanley Cup." A Stanley Cup champion with the St. Louis Blues, Perron has totaled 812 points (332 goals, 480 assists) in 1,239 career games with the Blues, Edmonton Oilers, Pittsburgh Penguins, Anaheim Ducks, Vegas Golden Knights, Red Wings and Senators. He was selected by St. Louis with the 26th overall pick of the 2007 NHL Draft. --Field Level Media

item.title: Trump move to restart direct US flights with Lebanon hits roadblock
item.description: The United Nations aviation agency has found Lebanon's main airport lacks valid certification, according to a report summary seen by Reuters, in a setback to US President Donald Trump's move to revive direct US-Beirut flights.
item.dc:creator: Allison Lampert, David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: The United Nations aviation agency has found Lebanon's main airport lacks valid certification, according to a report summary seen by Reuters, in a setback to US President Donald Trump's move to revive direct US-Beirut flights. Trump made the announcement in July and signed an order last month for [USN:FWN43N0RD TEXT:"the US government"] to allow direct flights from the US to Lebanon, reversing a four-decade-long suspension after TWA Flight 847 was hijacked and forced to land in Beirut in 1985. While the US Federal Aviation Administration and the Transportation Security Administration would still need to conduct safety reviews before flights could resume, the Lebanese embassy in Washington called Trump's order "a significant first step toward restoring direct air service between Lebanon and the United States." However, the UN's International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) technical assistance mission to Lebanon in July identified shortcomings at Beirut-Rafic Hariri International Airport and in the aviation system. The findings, which two senior industry officials familiar with the matter expect to delay the resumption of service, complicate efforts to follow up on an order Trump signed after meeting Lebanese President Joseph Aoun. Washington has backed Aoun as it pushes for Iran-backed Hezbollah to be disarmed. The agency sent its internal report, made at the request of the Lebanese Civil Aviation Authority (LCAA), to Lebanon in September. AIRPORT LACKS EMERGENCY PLAN: ICAO Beirut airport's firefighting resources are equipped for single-aisle planes, but not twin-aisle jetliners used for long-haul flights, according to a summary of ICAO's report. The airport also lacks an emergency plan, and its conditional certification has expired, the report said. "This is a serious and time-critical matter that must be addressed immediately to preserve the airport's operational status," the summary said. The report also found the Lebanese regulator LCAA lacks qualified inspectors to oversee air traffic control licensing, and has no fully established, operational and independent aircraft accident investigation authority with clearly defined roles. Such concerns were flagged during a two-day workshop last month where officials from ICAO, Lebanon's government, the FAA and others discussed efforts to revive direct air service, according to the industry officials and an agenda of the meeting seen by Reuters. Lebanon's Minister of Public Works and Transport Fayez Rasamny said Lebanon was taking steps to address the concerns, with efforts to certify the airport starting on Saturday. The LCAA expects to issue conditional certification in the coming days. "Most of the issues highlighted in the report had already been identified by the LCAA, and corrective action had already been initiated," Rasamny said in a statement, adding that progress had been delayed by war. Israeli forces remain in southern Lebanon and have continued strikes despite a US-brokered framework agreement signed in June between Israel and Lebanon. Hezbollah, which was not party to the deal, has rejected it. The FAA declined to comment. ICAO said it cannot comment on matters concerning specific countries, but said it conducts targeted analyses for member states. The US State Department advises Americans not to travel to Lebanon given safety concerns. It said the FAA advises caution for flights operating in Lebanese airspace due to heightened military activity in or around Syria, including the risks of errant long-range surface-to-air missiles originating from Syrian territory. MIDDLE EAST UNREST DISRUPTS AIR TRAVEL Foreign airlines have avoided large swathes of Middle East airspace because of missile and drone threats since US and Israeli strikes on Iran in February triggered regional hostilities, with an [USN:L6N4600LI TEXT:"airport"] in Saudi Arabia the latest site to come under attack. Lebanon and its national carrier have been praised domestically for maintaining air navigation services and flights, helping to prop up an economy that depends on tourism and remittances. Three US airline officials told Reuters on the condition of anonymity they do not think any American carriers would resume flights to Lebanon in the near term, citing security concerns. While there are no direct flights between Beirut and the United States, such service exists between Lebanon and some large European cities. The European Union Aviation Safety Agency said it was aware of the ICAO report and added that EU airlines must conduct their own assessment of an airport's safety and operational readiness before launching services.

item.title: Putin says Russia is building non-negotiable 'security zone' in Ukraine along border
item.description: Russia is establishing a "security zone" inside Ukraine along their border, which will be non-negotiable in any future talks with Kyiv, President Vladimir Putin said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russia is establishing a "security zone" inside Ukraine along their border, which will be non-negotiable in any future talks with Kyiv, President Vladimir Putin said on Friday. Putin, wearing military uniform and speaking during a visit to a command post, said the operation was in response to Ukraine's 2024-25 incursion into Russia's western Kursk region. "The Russian armed forces were tasked not only with expelling the enemy from our land but also with establishing a security zone in the adjacent territory. This task is being carried out successfully," he said in televised comments. "Our goal is to ensure the absolute security of Russia’s border regions for the future, and we do not plan to make this a subject for potential peace negotiations with Ukraine." Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the planned security zone spanned 660 km (410 miles), of which 70% was currently under Russia's control. He did not say how deep it would reach inside Ukraine. Putin has spoken before about the need for such a zone but has not previously spelt out the planned extent of it or said it would be off-limits for talks. It requires Russia to carve out land in the Sumy and Kharkiv regions, which are not among those it has claimed as its own territory since launching the war in Ukraine in 2022. Putin, who rarely dons military uniform, struck a hawkish and confident tone in his comments to senior officers. He was speaking at a critical point in diplomacy over the war , one week after a [USN:L4N45Y0AR TEXT:"deal"] to sell Russian diesel to the US that has won favour with President Donald Trump and prompted a new souring of the relationship between Trump and Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskiy. Putin said Russian forces had yet to capture just over 10% of the territory of Ukraine's Donetsk region, a key objective, and 16.5% of the Zaporizhzhia region. He praised the effectiveness of Russian strikes against Ukrainian military, industrial and logistics targets, while adding there was still room for improvement in Russia's own air defences. Ukrainian drones have attacked several Russian data centres and a big oil refinery in the past nine days, while Russia has continued to pound Ukrainian cities, power plants and ports, among other targets. Earlier, Putin's investment envoy Kirill Dmitriev said Russia and the US were discussing a range of new joint projects including [USN:L1N4620KW TEXT:"nuclear-powered data centres"] in the wake of last week's agreement on diesel.

item.title: Putin agrees to cooperate with Pope Leo's plea for aid for Ukrainian town
item.description: President Vladimir Putin told Pope Leo he had agreed to cooperate after the pontiff asked him on Friday to help get vital supplies into the Russian-controlled Ukrainian town of Oleshky, the Kremlin said.
item.dc:creator: Joshua McElwee
item.content:encoded: President Vladimir Putin told Pope Leo he had agreed to cooperate after the pontiff asked him on Friday to help get vital supplies into the Russian-controlled Ukrainian town of Oleshky, the Kremlin said. Leo phoned Putin and asked him to arrange a ceasefire to let aid and food into the town, taken by Russian forces in February 2022, the Vatican said. Residents have reported [USN:L8N45K1N1 TEXT:"a deepening food crisis"]. Leo expressed "deep concern" over the humanitarian situation there, the Vatican added. Russia and Ukraine accuse each other of blocking supplies to the town, which Ukrainian forces want to retake. "The Vatican’s intention to help create the conditions necessary to ensure the safety of the town’s population and to organise vital supplies has been supported," the Kremlin said in a statement. It did not mention a ceasefire. "It has been agreed to cooperate on this matter," it added. Leo and Putin are known to have spoken once previously, in June 2025. The pope also reaffirmed the Holy See's commitment to any initiatives for peace, the Vatican said. The pope, 71, is recovering at Rome's Gemelli hospital after surgery for lung cancer. The Vatican said earlier on Friday that he is [USN:L8N46210T TEXT:"showing steady improvement"] and is able to work and do normal daily activities. The Kremlin said Putin had wished Leo a speedy and full recovery. The Vatican's Secretary of State, Cardinal Pietro Parolin, told reporters after the call that it had been Leo's initiative. The pope, he said, wanted "to plead the cause of this besieged city". Russia has acknowledged critical problems with food and medical supplies in Oleshky and said its military was working to resolve them. It blamed Ukraine for the crisis, saying it was obstructing those supplies from getting to the town. Ukraine has said it is Russia which is thwarting food deliveries. Oleshky, in Ukraine's Kherson region, had a pre-war population of some 24,000, and is still home to around 1,700 residents, including 47 children, according to Danielle Bell, head of the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine.

item.title: Morocco's new government has new finance minister, keeps foreign, interior ministers unchanged
item.description: Morocco's football federation chief and former budget minister Fouzi Lekjaa was appointed economy and finance minister in the country's new government that was formed following the September 23 parliamentary elections, state news agency MAP reported.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed Eljechtimi
item.content:encoded: Morocco's football federation chief and former budget minister Fouzi Lekjaa was appointed economy and finance minister in the country's new government that was formed following the September 23 [USN:L8N45G056 TEXT:"parliamentary elections"], state news agency MAP reported. Lekjaa, a member of the liberal-centrist Authenticity and Modernity Party (PAM), joins a 32-member government led by Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, whom King Mohammed VI [USN:L8N45G056 TEXT:"appointed"] last month as the country's first woman head of government after PAM won the largest share of seats in parliament. PAM [USN:L1N45Y0PZ TEXT:"formed a coalition"] with moderate socialist parties PPS and USFP and the nationalist Istiqlal. Together they hold 207 seats in parliament, above the 198 needed for a majority. The new government retained the foreign affairs and interior ministers in their posts, MAP reported following the government appointment ceremony chaired by King Mohammed VI. The lineup also retained the ministers responsible for justice, water, defence, industry and transport. Among the newcomers, PPS leader Nabil Benabdallah returned to government as education minister, while fellow PPS member Charafat Afailal was named energy minister. Other newcomers included Khalid Hatimi as minister of agriculture, maritime fisheries and food sovereignty. The new government will oversee the final stages of a $20-billion push to prepare for [USN:L1N42004C TEXT:"the 2030 World Cup"], which Morocco will co-host with Portugal and Spain. It [USN:L6N4580D4 TEXT:"faces pressure"] to address unemployment and demands for better education and health services, which fuelled the youth [USN:L6N3VN095 TEXT:"Gen Z protests"] last year and the [USN:L1N43Y04J TEXT:"Ceuta migration crisis"] in July. [USN:L6N4580D4 TEXT:"The new government"], however, is not expected to change policy direction in Morocco, a constitutional monarchy where the king retains sweeping powers over foreign policy and defense.

item.title: US strikes one-year deal to fund maternal and newborn health donations in poorest countries
item.description: The US government has struck a deal to continue supplying some of the world's poorest nations with free life-saving medication and equipment for mothers, infants and young children, after months of uncertainty and challenges with supply.
item.dc:creator: Ammu Kannampilly, Jennifer Rigby, Victoire Mukenge
item.content:encoded: The US government has struck a deal to continue supplying some of the world's poorest nations with free life-saving medication and equipment for mothers, infants and young children, after [USN:L6N40L0RM TEXT:"months of uncertainty"] and challenges with supply. The UN children's agency UNICEF will now procure these items, a State department spokesperson told Reuters by email, without giving details of the arrangement. UNICEF said the agreement is worth $25 million and will last for one year. That sum represents only a small part of the aid affected by the Trump administration's cuts and dismantling of the US Agency for International Development (USAID). But it means that some of the world's most vulnerable nations will not face another abrupt disruption to supplies they relied on while they work on new health aid deals with the US. Nine former US aid officials, NGOs and government officials told Reuters that this had been a real concern because the deal the now-defunct USAID had with its contractor was due to run out last month. SHORTAGES The agreement covers the procurement and delivery of maternal and child health supplies, as well as some nutrition supplies, to at least 15 countries previously covered, including Democratic Republic of Congo, Haiti and Mali, UNICEF said. It follows almost 18 months of disruption after Washington's move to freeze and then scale back [USN:L2N3PI0VN TEXT:"many US aid programmes"] as part of its "America First Global Health Strategy". In countries such as Congo, shortages due to the disruption have already been showing up on the ground. At the Nyangezi General Hospital in eastern Congo, health workers said they had run out of supplies of life-saving medications including oxytocin to prevent and treat post-partum haemorrhage and amoxicillin, an antibiotic for paediatric use and during childbirth. "It was a donation we received (previously) from USAID, and at the moment, there is none," midwife Alice Bulambo told Reuters. The main government-run warehouse in the area has faced stockouts for over a year, said Olivier Kabarati Amani, chief medical officer for Nyangezi health zone. As a result, facilities are forced to buy medicines at market prices. Over the last six months, "the cost of care has doubled, if not tripled," Amani said, at a time when the healthcare system in eastern Congo is [USN:L6N45L142 TEXT:"already struggling"] with Ebola. The US State Department said it "has prioritized ensuring all life-saving commodities have continued to be made reliably available." TRANSITION Maternal and newborn health items amounted to less than 1% of the more than $5 billion spent by the USAID Global Health Supply Chain program between 2016 and 2023, according to the most recently available annual report. The spending was channelled through private contractor Chemonics. Reuters [USN:L6N40L0RM TEXT:"first reported"] on plans to close this programme, which also managed the donation and delivery of supplies to tackle malaria and HIV, in April, with aid officials warning that the September 30 shutdown could cause shortages. The plans to close the Chemonics supply chain are part of the broader US global health strategy, which aims to move countries towards self-reliance alongside scaled-back US support and reduced reliance on contractors. The US has instead signed more than 30 bilateral deals on health aid with recipient countries, including Congo, which require co-financing from the countries and are worth billions of dollars in total. But the details of the deals are still being worked out and it had been unclear what would fill the gap in the ordering procedure in the meantime. While many nations were already moving towards taking over their maternal and child health needs, lead times for orders can be a year or more, five former USAID officials said. The Congolese government aims to take over by next year, but has struggled with the recent uncertainty, said Polydor Kabila, coordinator of the universal healthcare programme in the president’s office. Alongside the UNICEF deal, the US authorities have extended the deadline for Chemonics deliveries of some key malaria and HIV items, the State Department spokesperson told Reuters. The US has also signed a deal with the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria to allow countries to order new US-funded HIV and malaria supplies through the Fund's order platform. In a statement, UNICEF said it would work with the US to "keep health and nutrition supplies moving so more children receive life-saving care," adding that no orders have yet been placed but are expected shortly.

item.title: Putin acepta petición del papa de ayuda para una localidad ucraniana
item.description: El presidente Vladimir Putin comunicó al papa León que había accedido a cooperar después de que el pontífice le pidió el viernes que ayude a hacer llegar suministros esenciales a la localidad ucraniana de Oleshky, controlada por Rusia, informó el Kremlin.
item.dc:creator: Joshua McElwee
item.content:encoded: El presidente Vladimir Putin comunicó al papa León que había accedido a cooperar después de que el pontífice le pidió el viernes que ayude a hacer llegar suministros esenciales a la localidad ucraniana de Oleshky, controlada por Rusia, informó el Kremlin. León llamó por teléfono a Putin y le pidió que organizara un alto el fuego para permitir la entrada de ayuda y alimentos en la localidad, tomada por las fuerzas rusas en febrero de 2022, informó el Vaticano. Los residentes han denunciado una crisis alimentaria cada vez más grave. León expresó su "profunda preocupación" por la situación humanitaria en la zona, añadió el Vaticano. Rusia y Ucrania se acusan mutuamente de bloquear el suministro de ayuda a la localidad, que las fuerzas ucranianas quieren recuperar. "Se ha respaldado la intención del Vaticano de ayudar a crear las condiciones necesarias para garantizar la seguridad de la población de la localidad y organizar el suministro de productos de primera necesidad", dijo el Kremlin en un comunicado, que no mencionó un alto el fuego. "Se ha acordado cooperar en este asunto", añadió. Se sabe que León y Putin ya habían hablado una vez antes, en junio de 2025. El papa también reafirmó el compromiso de la Santa Sede con cualquier iniciativa en favor de la paz, informó el Vaticano. El papa, de 71 años, se está recuperando en el hospital Gemelli de Roma tras someterse a una intervención quirúrgica por cáncer de pulmón. El Kremlin señaló que Putin había deseado a León una pronta y completa recuperación. El secretario de Estado del Vaticano, el cardenal Pietro Parolin, dijo a los periodistas que la conversación había sido una iniciativa de León. El papa, dijo, quería "abogar por la causa de esta ciudad sitiada". Rusia ha reconocido que existen problemas graves con los suministros alimentarios y médicos en Oleshky y ha dicho que sus fuerzas armadas están trabajando para resolverlos. Ha culpado a Ucrania de la crisis, alegando que está impidiendo que los suministros lleguen a la localidad. Ucrania, por su parte, ha afirmado que es Rusia la que está obstaculizando las entregas de alimentos. Oleshky, situada en la región ucraniana de Jersón, tenía antes de la guerra una población de unos 24.000 habitantes y aún alberga a unos 1.700 residentes, entre ellos 47 niños, según Danielle Bell, jefa de la Misión de Observación de los Derechos Humanos de Naciones Unidas en Ucrania.

item.title: Empleados Meta dicen que cuentas de Lula se vieron limitadas durante la elección: Folha
item.description: Empleados de Meta reconocieron en comunicaciones internas que las cuentas de Instagram del presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva se vieron afectadas negativamente por las restricciones impuestas durante las elecciones de Brasil, informó el viernes el periódico "Folha de S.Paulo", citando mensajes a los que tuvo acceso.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Empleados de Meta reconocieron en comunicaciones internas que las cuentas de Instagram del presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva se vieron afectadas negativamente por las restricciones impuestas durante las elecciones de Brasil, informó el viernes el periódico "Folha de S.Paulo", citando mensajes a los que tuvo acceso. Según el informe, los mensajes también reconocían que la plataforma recomendaba el perfil del candidato opositor, el senador Flávio Bolsonaro, así como su canal de WhatsApp. Meta dijo que los problemas técnicos mencionados en el artículo ya eran de dominio público y que las conversaciones a las que se hacía referencia eran únicamente sobre la gravedad de los problemas, y no una injerencia política. "Cualquier insinuación de que Meta favorece a una de las partes es falsa", añadió en un comunicado de la empresa. Lula se enfrentará a Bolsonaro en un balotaje el 25 de octubre, tras el resultado, mejor de lo esperado, obtenido por el senador en la primera vuelta celebrada a principios de este mes. El equipo de Lula afirmó a principios de esta semana que presentaría una denuncia ante la Organización de los Estados Americanos alegando que Meta, propietaria de Instagram, WhatsApp y Facebook, manipuló las redes sociales durante las elecciones de Brasil. Según el partido de Lula, algunas de sus publicaciones aparecieron sin botón para compartir, sufrieron una reducción de su alcance y presentaban historias que impedían las reacciones y el intercambio, además de aparecer sin audio o reproducirse a velocidad acelerada. Un magistrado del máximo tribunal electoral de Brasil ordenó el jueves a la empresa que no limitara injustificadamente el alcance del contenido político relacionado con ambos candidatos hasta el final de la campaña de la segunda vuelta. La resolución también estipulaba que Meta AI, el chatbot de inteligencia artificial de la empresa, no debe favorecer a ninguno de los candidatos a la hora de generar contenido relacionado con las elecciones.

item.title: Wall Street cae con fuerza presionado por las dudas sobre la IA y el alza del petróleo
item.description: Wall Street cerró el viernes con fuertes caídas, con CoreWeave, Broadcom y otras acciones tecnológicas relacionadas con la inteligencia artificial sometidas a una nueva presión, mientras que el repunte de los precios del petróleo inquietó a los operadores antes del fin de semana.
item.dc:creator: Noel Randewich
item.content:encoded: Wall Street cerró el viernes con fuertes caídas, con CoreWeave, Broadcom y otras acciones tecnológicas relacionadas con la inteligencia artificial sometidas a una nueva presión, mientras que el repunte de los precios del petróleo inquietó a los operadores antes del fin de semana. El Nasdaq amplió las pérdidas de principios de semana, arrastrado por la preocupación de que las empresas de infraestructura de IA, muy endeudadas, no puedan obtener ganancias a tiempo para saldar sus deudas, sobre todo ante la previsión de que aumenten los costos financieros. CoreWeave (CRWV.O) , respaldada por Nvidia, se desplomó, lo que se sumó a las pérdidas recientes. Los bonos del operador de centros de datos sufrieron una corriente vendedora esta semana, lo que elevó sus rendimientos a más del 15%. Broadcom (AVGO.O) también cayó y el índice de chips PHLX (.SOX) registró su octava jornada consecutiva de descensos. Los inversores también estuvieron pendientes de cómo los precios del petróleo subían más de un 3% debido a la preocupación por el suministro de Oriente Medio. "Hay cierto temor en el mercado", dijo Rob Haworth, estratega senior de inversiones de U.S. Bank Wealth Management. "Los altos precios del petróleo, en particular, tienden a presionar el múltiplo precio/beneficio de las acciones, por lo que creo que los inversores optan por mostrarse cautos antes del fin de semana en lugar de asumir más riesgos". A las preocupaciones por el financiamiento de la IA se suma que algunos inversores actuales y potenciales de Anthropic están considerando una valoración más baja para la empresa en su próxima salida a bolsa, según un reporte de Reuters, que citó a personas familiarizadas con el asunto. Según datos preliminares, el S&P 500 (.SPX) perdió 85,44 puntos, o un 1,10%, a 7.658,62 unidades, mientras que el Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) retrocedió 572,99 puntos, o un 2,15%, a 26.137,85. El Promedio Industrial Dow Jones (.DJI) cayó 189,01 puntos, o un 0,36%, a 51.990,05 unidades. La temporada de resultados del tercer trimestre sigue la próxima semana con las publicaciones de Tesla (TSLA.O) , Meta Platforms (META.O) y Procter & Gamble (PG.N) . Según datos de LSEG, los analistas prevén, en promedio, que las ganancias trimestrales se disparen más de un 30%, impulsadas por las grandes compañías relacionadas con la IA.

item.title: Meta employees said Lula's accounts were hindered during Brazil election, Folha reports
item.description: Meta employees acknowledged in internal communications that the Instagram accounts of Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva were hindered by restrictions during the country's election, newspaper Folha de S.Paulo reported on Friday, citing messages it reviewed.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Meta (META.O) employees acknowledged in internal communications that the Instagram accounts of Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva were hindered by restrictions during the country's election, newspaper Folha de S.Paulo reported on Friday, citing messages it reviewed. The messages also acknowledged the platform recommended the profile of challenger Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, as well as his WhatsApp channel, according to the report. Meta said the technical issues cited in the report were already public and the conversations it referenced related solely to the severity of the issues, not political interference. "Any suggestion that Meta favors one side is false," it added in a statement Lula will face Bolsonaro in a runoff on October 25, following a stronger-than-expected performance by the senator in the [USN:L6N45Q04L TEXT:"first-round vote"] earlier this month Lula's camp said earlier this week it would file a complaint before the Organization of American States alleging that Meta, which owns Instagram, WhatsApp and Facebook, manipulated social media during Brazil's election According to Lula's party, some of his posts appeared without a share button, suffered reduced reach, and had stories that prevented reactions and sharing, in addition to appearing without audio or playing at accelerated speed A justice at Brazil's top electoral court ordered the company on Thursday not to unjustifiably limit the reach of political content related to both candidates through the end of the runoff campaign The ruling also stipulated that Meta AI, the company's artificial intelligence chatbot, must not favor either candidate when generating election-related content

item.title: CDC reports 4,410 measles cases as outbreak grows
item.description: The US CDC on Friday reported 4,410 measles cases nationwide as of October 15, an increase of 330 from its last update a week ago, as an outbreak of the highly contagious disease continues.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The US CDC on Friday reported 4,410 measles cases nationwide as of October 15, an increase of 330 from its last update a week ago, as an outbreak of the highly contagious disease continues. Here are key details: Measles-related hospitalizations this year stand at 451, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said The state of Pennsylvania has reported five measles-related deaths The CDC has confirmed [USN:L4N45L13A TEXT:"two measles-associated deaths"] in 2026, though it has not identified the states involved Pennsylvania has reported 1,260 measles cases this year as of October 16, with 238 disease-related hospitalizations, according to state health department data Last month, the CDC [USN:L4N45A17G TEXT:"shifted"] to using mortality data from the National Center for Health Statistics for measles-related deaths, rather than relying on state health departments, a change that has drawn scrutiny The CDC [USN:L4N45Z1Q3 TEXT:"said"] on Tuesday it would deploy more support to Pennsylvania to help investigate the outbreak Children and teenagers aged 5 to 19 were the largest group affected by the disease at 1,856, or 42% of cases, followed by adults aged 20 and older at 1,787 cases, or 41%, CDC data showed Earlier this month, the state of New York [USN:L4N45R1BM TEXT:"declared"] a disaster emergency for the measles outbreak, the first such declaration by a US state

item.title: Zubimendi close to Arsenal return, Hincapie still sidelined, says Arteta
item.description: Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta said Martin Zubimendi could return for Sunday's Premier League match against Nottingham Forest, but Piero Hincapie is expected to remain sidelined after both players picked up injuries last week.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta said Martin Zubimendi could return for Sunday's Premier League match against Nottingham Forest, but Piero Hincapie is expected to remain sidelined after both players picked up injuries last week. The duo suffered ankle injuries during a training session following Arsenal's 2-1 win over Leeds United and were ruled out of Tuesday's Champions League victory over Lille “Piero (Hincapie) is evolving really well... I am sure it's not going to take long, but he will probably need another week or two," Arteta told reporters on Friday “Zubimendi looks much better... We have another session tomorrow, and after that we will assess whether he's available to play against Forest” Arsenal will also be without Christos Tzolis, who is recovering from a muscle injury sustained on international duty, and William Saliba, who remains sidelined with a back problem

item.title: Activos financieros argentinos cierran semana en baja
item.description: La plaza financiera de Argentina cerró en terreno negativo y con signos de prudencia el viernes, ante la cautela de inversores institucionales debido a recientes vaivenes del riesgo país y datos macroeconómicos domésticos.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La plaza financiera de Argentina cerró en terreno negativo y con signos de prudencia el viernes, ante la cautela de inversores institucionales debido a recientes vaivenes del riesgo país y datos macroeconómicos domésticos. Por su parte, en el contexto externo, las recientes declaraciones del presidente de la Reserva Federal (Fed), Kevin Warsh, generan incertidumbre sobre el devenir de las tasas de interés con impacto en las plazas emergentes. "Warsh pasó por Bangkok y evitó el único tema que el mercado quería escuchar. En una charla con Kristalina Georgieva (...) el presidente de la Fed no dedicó una sola línea a la política monetaria ni al panorama económico estadounidense", dijo Portfolio Personal Inversiones (PPI). Y añadió que "no se adelantó a decir que van a hacer en la reunión de octubre (...). Más allá de esto, el mercado espera con un 85% de probabilidad que mantengan inalterado el rango de tasas en octubre y lo suban recién en diciembre". En el ámbito local, el índice accionario S&P Merval (.MERV) de la bolsa de Buenos Aires cedió un 0,35% al cierre, mientras que los bonos en el segmento extrabursátil perdieron el 0,1% y cayeron un 0,9% en promedio durante la semana. El riesgo país argentino se afirmaba en la zona de 641 puntos básicos (2000 GMT), luego de oscilar recientemente entre un máximo de 650 unidades a inicios de mes y uno mínimo de 577 registrado la semana pasada como efecto del triunfo electoral de la derecha en Brasil. "Lo mejor que podemos esperar este año (del riesgo país es) que pueda terminar por debajo de los 500 puntos básicos", expresó en una entrevista el economista y docente Martín Polo. Remarcó que pese a los datos negativos de la actividad económica de julio, es "muy probable que los indicadores vengan un poco mejor y el Gobierno se ilusione", lo que podría ayudar a traer inversiones y mejorar el nivel del riesgo país. La tercera economía de América Latina viene de registrar en julio una contracción en su actividad económica (EMAE) de 1,4% interanual y de 2,9% en su medición desestacionalizada. Para agosto, economistas prevén que el EMAE arroje un resultado positivo. El dato oficial de la actividad económica se conocerá a mediados de la semana próxima. El peso argentino mayorista se depreció un 0,3% a 1.518 por dólar para la venta, con el habitual seguimiento de liquidez por parte del banco central (BCRA). La entidad monetaria sumó 68 millones de dólares este viernes y acumuló 642 millones para sus reservas a lo largo de esta semana corta por el feriado del lunes pasado.

item.title: In Yemen's besieged Taiz, families take shelter as Houthis close in
item.description: Ali Hassan and his family took shelter under a stairwell at a school in Taiz as Iran-allied Houthi forces closed in around them, tightening a siege of Yemen's third-largest city.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ali Hassan and his family took shelter under a stairwell at a school in Taiz as Iran-allied Houthi forces closed in around them, tightening a siege of [USN:L8N46125M TEXT:"Yemen's third-largest city"]. The 42-year-old said the latest fighting between the group and Saudi-backed government forces had forced him to flee several times. The wider conflict has also left its mark on his body: a shot from a Houthi sniper paralysed his hand in 2021, he said. "I only have my left hand," he told Reuters. A month ago, he added, another sniper shot his sister in the spine while she was herding sheep, leaving her completely disabled. Reuters could not verify his accounts. THEATRE IN WIDER REGIONAL WAR The city is fast becoming the most important front in Yemen's reignited civil war — itself a new theatre in the wider regional conflict that began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran in February. Houthi forces have encircled the city by cutting the main road south to Aden, forcing people from their homes and deepening a humanitarian crisis. A Houthi victory in Taiz would mark one of the biggest turning points in a war that resumed this summer after a four-year truce. The group denies being armed by Iran and says it is fighting a corrupt system in Yemen. Hassan said residents were facing Houthi fire and shortages of food and water as the group pushed for more territory. Last month, the Houthis tightened their grip on the Bab el-Mandeb shipping lane in a lightning advance. On Thursday, the group fired missiles at the presidential palace complex in the southern city of Aden, killing five people, the government said. The Saudi-led coalition has also listed dozens of Houthi [USN:L1N46209G TEXT:"attacks on Saudi infrastructure"] in recent weeks. The Aden strike and the Houthis' determination to take Taiz suggest the conflict could drag on, prolonging suffering in a city of almost 600,000. FOCAL POINT OF FIGHTING Taiz has been on the frontline between the Houthis and the government since the war's first days. It is now the last major urban stronghold of anti-Houthi forces in the southern highland area of Yemen. Resident Wathiq Mahyoub said prices were rising, fuel was running short and garbage was piling up on the streets. "The siege is suffocating. It's strangling the citizens," Mahyoub told Reuters. "The Houthis refused to open the crossing for us, even to dump the rubbish." War broke out in Yemen in 2014 when the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa, driving the government south to Aden. A Saudi-led military intervention the following year led to a bloody stalemate before a 2022 truce that held until this year. Last week, government forces launched a campaign to recapture areas controlled by the Houthis, recovering ground near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a key shipping artery. Aid agencies have warned of rapidly worsening conditions in Yemen. HUMANITARIAN CRISIS "There are no camps equipped to receive these families. We find some of these families living in large unfinished buildings," said Ahmed al-Jalal, director of the Executive Unit for the Management of Displaced Persons' Camps, Al-Muzaffar district, in Taiz governorate. "Some are in shops, some in buildings unfit for living, with no essentials for living," he added. Speaking to reporters in Geneva, Zoe Brennan, spokesperson for the UN migration agency, said 233,077 people have been displaced so far in the latest conflict, 121,530 of them in Taiz. World Health Organization spokesperson Tarik Jašarević said 12 hospitals had about four days of fuel while there was a shortage of oxygen and medicines. "Taiz is being cut off, and its hospitals are running out of supplies as fighting has reached urban districts where the main referral hospitals stand," he said. "Unfortunately, the road closures are blocking the resupply."

item.title: US solicits exchange of up to 17 million barrels of oil from strategic reserve
item.description: The United States has issued a request for proposal for an exchange of up to 17 million barrels of crude oil from the nation's Strategic Petroleum Reserve, the Department of Energy said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The United States has issued a request for proposal for an exchange of up to 17 million barrels of crude oil from the nation's Strategic Petroleum Reserve, the Department of Energy said on Friday. The exchange would be part of a global deal [USN:FWN3ZY1GJ TEXT:"the US struck in March"] to try to control fuel prices impacted by the Iran war . Washington agreed then to loan 172 million barrels of oil from the SPR as part of a wider deal with about 30 countries in the International Energy Agency to release 400 million barrels from reserves around the world. The US has released about 132.5 million barrels from the SPR since the US-Iran war began. The latest 17 million barrel round would be a portion of the pending 40 million barrels of oil that would be the last batch of the release. The Department of Energy had offered the 40 million barrels in June, but revealed later that month that companies agreed to borrow only about 500,000 barrels. The government offered those barrels again in late September. While the Department of Energy has not published the awards from that round, Friday's announcement implies that around 23 million barrels were awarded in the September round, research and consultancy Energy Aspects wrote in a note.

item.title: Starlink disruptions are being felt on the front lines of Ukraine
item.description: For one artillery unit fighting in eastern Ukraine, the US decision this week to reduce services provided by satellite company Starlink to the military had an immediate impact.
item.dc:creator: Sergiy Chalyi
item.content:encoded: For one artillery unit fighting in eastern Ukraine, the US [USN:L1N4610ZC TEXT:"decision"] this week to reduce services provided by satellite company Starlink to the military had an immediate impact. Communications with headquarters were interrupted and internet speeds dropped, posing risks in a war where drones present a constant danger and up-to-date information on targets and threats can make the difference between life and death. "Immediately after the announcement that the connection with Starlink was deteriorating, it really did have a negative impact," said Ukrlan, a 28-year-old serving with an artillery unit of the Special Rifle Police Battalion. He asked to be identified only by his callsign, in keeping with Ukrainian military practice. "We felt it straight away," he told Reuters from his bunker near the front line in the fiercely contested region of Donbas. "The internet speed at our position had deteriorated significantly and communication with our headquarters and our command had deteriorated significantly." According to officials, the White House issued an order to limit SpaceX's Starshield satellite system used by Ukraine for battlefield communications and drone operations. A US official has denied that President Donald Trump ordered a deliberate slowdown of Starshield, and Trump said this week intelligence sharing with Ukraine continued. Ukraine and its Western partners [USN:L1N46209U TEXT:"decried"] the slowdown as aiding Russia in the war, which began nearly five years ago with Moscow's full-scale invasion . The US says it wants to end the war and is working towards doing so.
