While much of the focus has been on Starshield, the military-grade version of SpaceX's Starlink service, Ukrlan's comments point to broader disruptions affecting internet connectivity and speeds. ROAR OF THE GUN Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy [USN:S8N4390AY TEXT:"told leaders"] in Brussels on Friday that Starlink services had improved but had not yet been fully restored, which he said put civilian lives at risk. "Starlink is really necessary for Ukraine. And unfortunately, in short term, Europe can't replace this capability," said the EU's foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas. Ukrlan's unit had been firing a howitzer at Russian targets from a heavily camouflaged position dug deep into the ground. Soldiers hurriedly prepared shells in a dark, timber-framed bunker by the light of head torches, covering their ears each time the gun roared and filled the space with smoke. Ukrainian soldiers have said slower Starlink speeds have impaired the military's ability to detect and intercept incoming missiles and drones. The US move to temporarily restrict the system came as President Donald Trump has pressured Kyiv to stop its attacks on Russian oil refineries. He has blamed those strikes for soaring energy prices that are denting his Republican Party's prospects in the November midterm elections , although experts say that the spike is mainly the result of the US war with Iran. For Ukrainians, the consequences of his approach are clear. "At first he insisted very strongly that he would help us bring it to an end in a very short space of time," Ukrlan said, referring to Trump's promise to end the Ukraine war soon after his return to office. "But we haven't seen any sign of that at all. And things are just getting worse every day, every week."

item.title: Dólar se encamina a caída semanal por menor expectativa de alza de tasas de la Fed
item.description: El dólar bajó el viernes, en camino a su primera caída semanal en más de un mes frente al euro y al yen, en medio de menores expectativas de un alza de tasas de interés de la Reserva Federal y preocupaciones por una ola de ventas en las bolsas impulsada por la inteligencia artificial.
item.dc:creator: Laura Matthews
item.content:encoded: El dólar bajó el viernes, en camino a su primera caída semanal en más de un mes frente al euro y al yen, en medio de menores expectativas de un alza de tasas de interés de la Reserva Federal y preocupaciones por una ola de ventas en las bolsas impulsada por la inteligencia artificial. * Los mercados se vieron sacudidos esta semana por datos de precios al consumo y a la producción más altos de lo esperado. * No obstante, las autoridades de la Fed aseguraron que no hay urgencia por endurecer la política monetaria, contribuyendo a estabilizar el rendimiento de los bonos del Tesoro y minando el apoyo al dólar. * Las acciones del sector de la IA cayeron esta semana y la tensión se extendió a sectores del mercado crediticio, ya que los inversores a lo largo de toda la cadena de suministro temen ahora que los operadores de centros de datos no logren ser rentables a tiempo para pagar sus deudas. * El índice dólar , que compara al billete verde con una cesta de seis destacadas divisas, cayó un 0,17% a 101,87 unidades, en camino a un descenso semanal del 0,35%. * La libra esterlina ganó un 0,31%, a 1,3314 dólares, con un alza acumulada del 0,63% en la semana, mientras que el dólar restó un 0,25% ante el franco suizo, al 0,8246%, lo que supone un declive semanal del 0,67%. * El euro subió un 0,08%, a 1,1227 dólares, tras mejorar un 0,56% el jueves, su mayor avance diario en dos meses y en camino a un alza semanal del 0,48%. Frente al yen, el dólar cedió un 0,08%, a 158,11 unidades, cerca de poner fin a cuatro semanas seguidas a la baja.

item.title: Why is the battle for Yemen's Taiz so important?
item.description: The city of Taiz is rapidly emerging as the most important battlefront in Yemen's reignited civil war, pitting the Iran-allied Houthis against the internationally recognised government, which is backed by a Saudi-led coalition.
item.dc:creator: Angus Mcdowall
item.content:encoded: The city of Taiz is rapidly emerging as the most important battlefront in Yemen's [USN:L6N45S0PX TEXT:"reignited civil war"], pitting the Iran-allied [USN:L1N45Q02Z TEXT:"Houthis"] against the internationally recognised government, which is backed by a Saudi-led coalition. Houthi forces have [USN:L1N45Z0S1 TEXT:"encircled Taiz"] in recent weeks by cutting its main road south to Aden, causing widespread displacement and worsening a humanitarian crisis. Here's what you need to know: WHY IS TAIZ SO IMPORTANT? Any Houthi victory in Taiz, Yemen's third-largest city, would mark one of the biggest turning points in the country's long civil war, which resumed this summer after a four-year truce. Taiz city has an estimated population of almost 600,000, said Katja Juric, Aden-based head of programmes for the International Organization for Migration (IOM). Government sources said 80,000 had fled in the latest fighting. Taiz has been on the frontline between the Houthis and the government since the first days of the conflict that started in early 2015 and has long been seen as a bastion of opposition to the Iran-allied group. It is the last major urban stronghold of anti-Houthi forces in the southern highland area of Yemen: the rugged hills above both Aden, where the internationally recognised government is based, and the flat coastal plain around the [USN:L8N4520BL TEXT:"Bab el-Mandeb"] Strait. A Houthi takeover of Taiz would make it much harder for government forces to maintain their counterattack around Bab el-Mandeb and keep the Houthis at arm's length from Aden. It would also mean a resounding symbolic defeat for the government and the military coalition of Saudi-backed Yemeni forces fighting the Houthis. WHAT'S THE MILITARY SITUATION AROUND TAIZ? For years the city has sat at the tip of a government salient stretching north into Houthi territory. The Houthis held areas to the north, east and west of Taiz, while government forces had the city and its immediate surroundings including Jebel Sabar, the high mountain rising above it to the south. As fighting in Yemen resumed in recent weeks, the Houthis began making advances to cut off Taiz by seizing territory to the south of Jebel Sabar along the road to Aden, which snakes about 200 km (125 miles) through rugged hills where fighting is slow and difficult. Sections of the road are now under Houthi control, including at the towns of al-Turbah and Mudiriyat al-Misrakh, leaving Taiz encircled since early October, with the Houthis sometimes shelling government positions in and around the city. Government forces, backed by airstrikes from the Saudi-led coalition, are trying to drive the Houthis back from their recent gains and reopen the road, but were still losing ground around Taiz rather than recapturing territory in mid-October. WHY IS TAIZ A STRONGHOLD OF OPPOSITION TO THE HOUTHIS? Taiz had a long history of difficult ties with rulers from north Yemen and was a hotbed of the 2011 Arab Spring uprisings that toppled veteran former president Ali Abdullah Saleh. While the Houthis adhere to the Zaydi school of Shi'ite Islam, Taiz is predominantly Sunni Muslim. Saleh and the Houthis joined forces to seize the capital, Sanaa, in 2014, derailing a political transition that arose out of the Arab Spring and had led to a proposal for a federal, democratic state. In early 2015, army units loyal to Saleh seized positions in the city, leading to big protests there followed by armed clashes. Protesters accused Saleh and the Houthis of mounting a coup d'etat. Months of fierce fighting in and around the city followed, with the Houthis and Saleh's army units battling local fighters and army brigades from Yemen's now fragmented military that backed the government. Taiz citizens endured shelling, sniper fire and terrible shortages in a long siege before government forces eventually drove the Houthis and their allies from the city and re-established a land route to Aden. The fighting in the city lasted throughout 2015 and parts of 2016, and the siege ran for long stretches until 2017. WHAT IS THE HUMANITARIAN SITUATION IN TAIZ? The latest fighting has displaced at least 121,000 in Taiz province, according to the IOM, though many of these are from rural areas outside the city. Inside Taiz, residents have told Reuters about the shortages they now face of basic items and the huge increase in prices they see in the city markets since the Houthis cut the road to Aden. Aid agencies have reported widespread shortages of fuel, food, medicines and clean water. Wheat flour stocks in the city are nearly exhausted, the World Food Programme said in mid-October. The situation risks worsening existing health problems. The UN children's agency UNICEF recently found that one in three of the children it screened in Yemen was malnourished. Cholera, dengue and malaria are all present in Yemen too. WHAT HAPPENS NEXT? Government forces backed by Saudi airstrikes are still trying to take back territory to reopen the road, but there is no guarantee they will succeed. The Houthis, who have [USN:L1N46209G TEXT:"upped their attacks"] on Saudi targets while showing themselves [USN:L6N4580DE TEXT:"better armed"] and organised than in earlier phases of the war, are meanwhile trying to cement their siege of Taiz and move closer towards the city. That might lead to a prolonged siege of the kind that Taiz experienced in the earlier phase of the war. It's also possible the Houthis might try to take the city. Local opposition means resistance could be fierce and any such attempt could cause a long, bloody battle.

item.title: Wall Street ends down sharply, worries about AI trade and high oil prices weigh
item.description: Wall Street ended sharply lower on Friday, with CoreWeave, Broadcom and other AI-related technology stocks under renewed pressure, while a jump in oil prices spooked traders heading into the weekend.
item.dc:creator: Noel Randewich
item.content:encoded: Wall Street ended sharply lower on Friday, with CoreWeave, Broadcom and other AI-related technology stocks under renewed pressure, while a jump in oil prices spooked traders heading into the weekend. The Nasdaq extended losses from earlier in the week, hammered by concerns that debt-laden AI infrastructure companies may not turn profits in time to repay debts, particularly with borrowing costs expected to rise. [USN:L6N4620IB TEXT:"Nvidia-backed"] CoreWeave (CRWV.O) slumped 12%, bringing its loss over the past five sessions to about 25%. The data center operator's bonds also sold off sharply this week, pushing yields above 15%. Broadcom (AVGO.O) fell 4.5%, and the PHLX chip index (.SOX) sank 3.8% in its eighth straight day of declines, its longest losing streak since 2008. Investors on Friday were also watching oil prices jump more than 3% due to Middle East supply worries. "There is some fear in the market," said Rob Haworth, senior investment strategist at U.S. Bank Wealth Management in Seattle. "High oil prices, in particular, tend to weigh on the price/earnings multiple of stocks, and so I think you have investors looking to be cautious into the weekend rather than take more risk." Adding to concerns around AI financing, some current Anthropic investors and prospective investors [USN:L6N4611DN TEXT:"are weighing a lower valuation"] for the company in its upcoming IPO, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter. The S&P 500 declined 1.09% to end the session at 7,659.44 points. The Nasdaq declined 2.15% to 26,140.03 points, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average dipped 0.34% to 52,002.41 points. Reflecting a rotation from tech stocks into other areas of the stock market, six of the S&P 500's 11 sector indexes rose, led by energy (.SPNY) , up 2.47%, followed by a 1.4% gain in utilities (.SPLRCU) . Volume on US exchanges was relatively heavy, with 18.6 billion shares traded, compared to an average of 17.7 billion shares over the previous 20 sessions. For the week, the S&P 500 fell almost 1.95% and the Nasdaq slumped 4.48%, their deepest weekly declines since June. The Dow climbed 0.67% for the week. Third-quarter earnings season shifts into high gear next week with reports from Tesla (TSLA.O) , Meta Platforms (META.O) and Procter & Gamble (PG.N) . Analysts on average see quarterly earnings surging more than 30%, driven by AI-related megacaps, according to LSEG data. While the S&P 500 remains up about 12% in 2026, most of that gain has come from AI-related tech stocks, and the index’s median component has climbed only about 6%, year to date. About 185 S&P 500 stocks have lost ground in 2026. Hotter-than-expected consumer and producer inflation reports this week showed price pressures were extending beyond energy commodities. Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh on Friday [USN:L6N462084 TEXT:"voiced optimism"] about US economic strength and surprise about how well global economies have been "hanging in there" during a lingering energy shock and tighter monetary policy to fight inflation. Markets increasingly expect the Fed to keep interest rates unchanged this month. Barclays [USN:FWN4622T4 TEXT:"now expects"] 25-basis-point hikes each in December and January. Tesla (TSLA.O) dropped 3.1% after the electric-vehicle maker unveiled a [USN:L1N46200L TEXT:"redesigned Roadster"], powered by rocket-style thrusters, developed in collaboration with SpaceX. item.description: Los precios del petróleo subieron más de un 3% para registrar un avance semanal, debido a la continua incertidumbre sobre el suministro en Oriente Medio, mientras los inversionistas seguían evaluando la cantidad de gasóleo que Rusia podría suministrar a los mercados mundiales.
item.dc:creator: Arathy Somasekhar
item.content:encoded: Los precios del petróleo subieron más de un 3% para registrar un avance semanal, debido a la continua incertidumbre sobre el suministro en Oriente Medio, mientras los inversionistas seguían evaluando la cantidad de gasóleo que Rusia podría suministrar a los mercados mundiales. * Los futuros del crudo Brent se disparaban 3 dólares a un máximo de sesión de 109,58 dólares el barril a las 1650 GMT, mientras que los futuros del crudo West Texas Intermediate (WTI) de Estados Unidos sumaban 3 dólares a un pico de jornada de 101,02 dólares y un máximo desde el 21 de septiembre. En lo que va de semana, el Brent ha subido alrededor de un 4% y el WTI un 8,5%. "El conflicto en Oriente Medio sigue reapareciendo y creo que es cuestionable la cantidad de gasóleo que Rusia puede suministrar realmente a los mercados. Esos dos factores siguen impulsando a los operadores a comprar", afirmó Dennis Kissler, vicepresidente sénior de operaciones de BOK Financial. * La inquietud por el suministro también aumentó al recrudecer los ataques en torno al estrecho de Ormuz durante los últimos 10 días, y con Irán afirmando que está intensificando los ataques en respuesta al bloqueo estadounidense de sus puertos y a las sanciones más duras introducidas el mes pasado. * Los hutíes lanzaron el jueves misiles contra el complejo del palacio presidencial de Yemen, en la ciudad sureña de Adén, matando a dos guardias, mientras que la coalición liderada por Arabia Saudita en Yemen detalló decenas de ataques contra infraestructuras saudíes en el marco de este conflicto cada vez más intenso. "La intensificación de los ataques iraníes provocó una fuerte caída de los flujos de crudo del Golfo", dijeron analistas de Kpler en un reporte el jueves, añadiendo que esperan una recuperación más lenta y desigual de los flujos por el estrecho de Ormuz a falta de un acuerdo político global. Mientras tanto, Ucrania atacó el jueves una refinería de petróleo rusa después de que el presidente Volodimir Zelenski declarara que Kiev abandonaba el alto el fuego sobre las instalaciones energéticas anunciado por el presidente Donald Trump y criticara la disposición de este último a llegar a acuerdos con Moscú. La refinería de petróleo rusa de Riazán ha suspendido las operaciones en una unidad de destilación primaria de crudo tras un ataque con drones en la región el jueves, informaron dos fuentes del sector a Reuters. La AIE acordó el jueves liberar más de 20 millones de barriles de combustible al mercado.

item.content:encoded: Britain's financial watchdog said on Friday it had revoked bans on four former traders previously sanctioned over the LIBOR and EURIBOR manipulation scandal after the Court of Appeal overturned their convictions earlier this month. item.title: Israeli settlers burn olive trees, injure journalist in West Bank attack
item.description: Clad in black and their faces masked, dozens of militant Israeli settlers burned olive trees and threw rocks at Palestinians in a coordinated attack on Friday on a village's harvest in the Israeli-occupied West Bank that injured at least two people, including a journalist.
item.dc:creator: Pesha Magid, Ali Sawafta
item.content:encoded: Clad in black and their faces masked, dozens of militant Israeli settlers burned olive trees and threw rocks at Palestinians in a coordinated attack on Friday on a village's harvest in the Israeli-occupied West Bank that injured at least two people, including a journalist. Some 80 settlers, some of them carrying gas canisters, descended from a hill above a terraced olive grove where villagers from Abu Falah had gathered to pick ripe fruit, a cherished annual tradition in Palestinian life, Reuters witnesses said. The settlers took positions in front of the terraced lanes of olive trees. Some of them used slings to launch rocks towards Palestinian villagers, who descended towards the bottom of the hill before picking up and throwing stones to defend themselves. "The settlers want to attack us and force us from our homes," said Moutaz Abdelhadi, 42, a farmer who witnessed the attack in Abu Falah. Partway through the attack, at least two Israeli military jeeps sped through the area, kicking up dust as villagers ran out of their way. The attack continued after the military's arrival, with Israeli soldiers firing tear gas in the direction of the Palestinians who had dodged the jeeps. The sound of live gunfire could be heard in the area, and a Reuters photographer saw at least one armed settler fire a gun. In a statement, the Israeli military said soldiers and border police fired what it described as warning shots after deploying to the area and at one point fired towards a person who the troops believed had posed a threat. "Attempts to incite friction between populations undermine security in the area," the military said. "Attacks and violence against innocent civilians are grave and unacceptable," it added. WASHINGTON POST JOURNALIST INJURED Palestinian medics said two people were injured and taken to hospitals in the area of Ramallah. One of them was Heidi Levine, an American photojournalist with the Washington Post. Video of the attack showed Levine lying on her side on a dirt path with her hands over her face as at least three settlers surrounded her. Speaking from a hospital bed later, Levine, who is in stable condition, said: "I was attacked, pushed to the ground. Luckily I had my flak jacket and helmet, otherwise I probably wouldn't even be here, because they just kept kicking me and kicking me." Levine said the attack ended when her Palestinian colleagues intervened, after which medics rushed her in an ambulance to a clinic in Abu Falah and then to hospital in Ramallah. Her voice shook as she spoke, and she had bandages over her left hand. The Washington Post later reported she suffered lacerations across her body and a broken rib, and would need surgery on one hand after a finger was ripped open, exposing bone. In a statement, Matt Murray, the Washington Post's executive editor, called for an investigation into the incident. "This morning, a Washington Post photographer, Heidi Levine, was attacked by Israeli settlers while reporting in the West Bank,” Murray said. "She was wearing visible markings clearly identifying her as a journalist. While we are relieved that Heidi has received medical care and is safe, we are outraged by this unwarranted attack on a journalist doing her job and urge a thorough investigation and follow-through from authorities." The US State Department said it condemned criminal violence by any party in the West Bank and supported holding the perpetrators accountable. "The Department of State is aware of these reports. We are greatly concerned when any American is harmed overseas and stand ready to provide all appropriate consular assistance," a department spokesperson said. The department has reached out to the Washington Post to offer consular assistance, he added. SETTLER VIOLENCE HAS SURGED IN WEST BANK Israeli settler violence against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank has surged, with at least 170 attacks since September 27, around the start of the annual olive harvest, according to Yesh Din, an Israeli settlements monitoring group. The settlers have been emboldened by the right-wing government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who has overseen a rapid expansion of settlements and smaller outposts across the West Bank. Netanyahu has criticized the violence but has taken few steps to crack down on incidents that have drawn international condemnation and sanction plans by longtime Israeli allies, including Britain. In a statement, Netanyahu’s office said the incident was under investigation. The West Bank is home to some 500,000 settlers and at least 3 million Palestinians. UN bodies and most countries deem the settlements illegal under international law regarding military occupations. Israel rejects this, viewing the territory as disputed rather than occupied. The Abu Falah attack followed a similar attack on Friday morning in the area of Turmus Ayya village, where settlers burned three cars after attacking a group of farmers harvesting olives. The military did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Salah Abu Niswa, who witnessed the attack in Turmus Ayya, said the settlers "snuck up like thieves, they caught someone by himself and began to beat him."

item.title: Beijing seeks tighter grip on AI exports amid US rivalry
item.description: China proposed export controls on 23 AI technologies.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Baptista
item.content:encoded: China proposed export controls on 23 AI technologies on Friday, including those involving models, agents and computing clusters, its latest move to limit transfers of tools it views as vital to national security and geopolitical competition with Washington. The proposals cover overseas deployment of AI models containing restricted technology, but exclude access through application programming interfaces (APIs), websites, apps and software-as-a-service platforms, China's commerce ministry said. The distinction could allow Chinese AI developers such as DeepSeek and Alibaba to continue expanding internationally while giving Beijing greater oversight of transfers of sensitive AI technology abroad. Chinese AI models have gained ground abroad on the back of lower prices and improving capabilities since DeepSeek's R1 model emerged early last year, raising the stakes for Beijing as it decides how tightly to guard the sector. Reuters reported in July that Chinese authorities had discussed with major technology companies, including Alibaba, ByteDance and Z.AI, [USN:L1N4390BM TEXT:"potentially restricting overseas access"] to China's most advanced AI models, including unreleased ones. PREVENTING AI FROM HARMING NATIONAL SECURITY The [USN:L4N43W34R TEXT:"capabilities"] of frontier models like Anthropic's Mythos have highlighted the potential for AI to turbocharge cyberattacks, worrying Beijing and prompting Chinese companies to seek to develop their own versions. Washington's export controls on China's access to cutting-edge American AI chips needed to train frontier models have so far helped keep US firms Anthropic and OpenAI in the lead, though Chinese rivals are finding workarounds to narrow the gap. While both countries strive to lead in AI, some bilateral efforts are underway to address existential risks posed by the technology. The two powers have agreed to keep humans in control of nuclear-weapons decisions and last month set up a dialogue and an incident-communications channel for advanced AI. The commerce ministry said on Friday the controls were partly intended to prevent misuse of AI technologies, including systems capable of autonomously generating and modifying malicious software that could threaten critical infrastructure and national security. It said most AI technologies would remain freely exportable, with simplified licensing for open-source technology exports and Chinese companies operating their own computing centres overseas. Technology already in the public domain through open-source releases or academic papers would be outside the proposed controls. BROADER REVISION The proposals form part of a broader revision of China's technology export catalogue, covering 40 technologies across AI, biotechnology and solar power. The proposals also include prohibiting the transfer of intellectual property ownership involving some novel cell and gene therapies and small interfering RNA (siRNA) technologies. Exporters must register certain overseas technology transfers from Friday, pending final rules after public consultation on the proposals closes November 15.

item.title: Rogue AI agents broke into Indian firms' live systems, government says
item.description: AI models under test broke into Indian organisations' live systems and read confidential records undetected, India's cybersecurity agency said, the country's first such official account after similar incidents of rogue AI behavior worldwide.
item.dc:creator: Munsif Vengattil
item.content:encoded: AI models under test broke into Indian organisations' live systems and read confidential records undetected, India's cybersecurity agency said, the country's first such official account after similar incidents of rogue AI behavior worldwide. AI model providers had voluntarily disclosed that their agents "exceeded the authorisation of their assigned tasks" during test runs to access Indian firms' data, including business records, the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) said late on Thursday. It did not name the providers or the affected organisations. The disclosure brings India into a growing global debate over how AI companies test models with advanced hacking abilities. OpenAI said in July its models [USN:L6N45604D TEXT:"went rogue"] during testing and breached a startup, while Anthropic has disclosed at least four [USN:L4N4511Q1 TEXT:"instances"] of AI models' hacking external systems so far this year. OpenAI has also [USN:L4N45L03J TEXT:"apologised"] for the hacking of an Australian government website by its rogue AI agent. None of the affected Indian entities detected the intrusions themselves, and in every case it was the AI companies that flagged the incidents, CERT-In said. In a second set of cases, the government agency's own investigations found attackers deliberately using freely available AI tools to probe Indian systems and break in for financial gain, with such tools deployed widely across infrastructure in multiple countries. Attacks that once took days from first entry to final damage were compressed to a few hours, CERT-In said, and victims that failed to fully clean up were attacked again within days, at greater depth.

item.title: Ambani's Reliance breaks silence on Musk, says Jio awaits same clearances as Starlink
item.description: Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani's Reliance said it welcomed competition from Elon Musk's Starlink and that its own satellite services were also awaiting clearance, its first response to accusations that Ambani was blocking Starlink's India launch.
item.dc:creator: Munsif Vengattil
item.content:encoded: Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani's Reliance said it welcomed competition from Elon Musk's Starlink and that its own satellite services were also awaiting clearance, its first response to accusations that Ambani was blocking Starlink's India launch. Musk, the world's richest man, has repeatedly [USN:L4N45V0R8 TEXT:"accused"] the Indian government and Ambani of stalling Starlink's years-long efforts to launch in a market of more than a billion internet subscribers. India has [USN:L4N45U09O TEXT:"denied any bias"] in its approval process. The Friday statement, which did not name Musk, comes days before Reliance Industries' (RELI.NS) digital unit Jio Platforms seeks [USN:L1N4600N0 TEXT:"a $108 billion valuation"] in India's largest IPO to date. Jio houses Reliance's telecom arm, which has over 530 million customers and is a potential competitor to Starlink in India's internet market. "At Reliance, we have never feared competition," the conglomerate said on Friday, addressing "remarks about Reliance and the Indian market" in a statement it said was intended to "place the facts on record". Starlink responded on Friday saying it had worked with Indian regulators and the industry for more than five years and had built dedicated systems, gateways and other infrastructure in the country with the required government approvals. "Starlink is ready to connect India with high-speed internet," the company said on X. In a separate post responding to Reliance, Musk said: "Much appreciated". INDIA'S LONG WAIT FOR SATELLITE INTERNET Musk's posts on X have ranged from asking whether Ambani was the "real boss" of India to addressing him as "Prime Minister Ambani" and asking whether he would allow Starlink to compete. The attacks mark a sharp turn for Musk, who has a warm public rapport with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, and come as New Delhi courts foreign investment and negotiates a trade deal with Washington. India has licensed Starlink, Jio's satellite internet arm and Bharti-backed Eutelsat OneWeb to operate services, but none has the security clearance needed to launch. Satellite broadband could help to connect hundreds of millions of Indians who remain offline, mostly in rural and remote areas. Musk has said he would price Starlink [USN:L4N45X012 TEXT:"affordably"] in India to take on Jio's low-cost internet plans. Cheap data is how Jio built its presence in India, and Musk has used the same strategy in markets like Kenya to disrupt local telecom players.

item.title: Stocks slip as dollar heads for weekly loss
item.description: Global stocks fell modestly on Friday as markets stabilised after a sharp tech-led selloff, while the dollar headed for a weekly loss.
item.dc:creator: Chibuike Oguh, Elizabeth Howcroft
item.content:encoded: Global stocks fell modestly on Friday as markets stabilised after a sharp tech-led selloff, while the dollar headed for a weekly loss. Markets have been [USN:L1N46113N TEXT:"rattled"] this week by concerns over higher interest rates and the debt-fuelled financing behind the AI boom, triggering a selloff in technology and chip stocks. Traders increased bets on further US rate hikes after [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"stronger-than-expected"] inflation data was released on Wednesday, while investors piled into Treasuries and other government bonds. On Wall Street, the benchmark S&P 500 and the Nasdaq were trading down and were headed for weekly losses. The Dow was lower after reversing early gains but was still set for a weekly gain. Technology and communication services were driving losses while the top gainers were utilities and energy stocks. CoreWeave's (CRWV.O) shares shed 13% and were on track to lose nearly 26% this week amid increasing investor scrutiny of the financing for the massive AI infrastructure buildout. The Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) fell 0.57%, the S&P 500 (.SPX) lost 1.3%, and the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) fell 2.3%. The MSCI World Equity Index lost 0.54% and was set for a weekly loss (.MIWD00000PUS) . European stock indexes, [USN:L1N461090 TEXT:"hit less hard"] by Thursday's selloff, gained, with the STOXX 600 adding 0.72% (.STOXX) . London's FTSE 100 (.FTSE) rose 0.38%. "We're starting to see some cracks in the financing of data centers because you're not too sure who's going to be the winners," said Tom Plumb, portfolio manager at Plumb Balanced Fund. "Our view is that there's going to be some really significant winners. But you have to be careful on the financing capability because companies don't get into trouble because their assets don't exceed their liabilities. They get into trouble when they have liquidity issues." [USN:L1N462067 TEXT:"Asian stocks"] mostly rose, and bond markets steadied, with investors reversing some of the previous session's moves. Indonesian equities suffered their [USN:L4N46124S TEXT:"biggest drop since 1998"] after index provider MSCI said the country's market no longer merited emerging-market status and outlined plans to remove it from key indexes tracked by funds. DOLLAR FALLS, BONDS RECOVER The dollar index fell 0.21% and was on track for its first weekly decline after four weeks of gains, as lower Treasury yields reduced the currency's appeal. Further worries about AI would push the dollar down further, [USN:L1N46204G TEXT:"analysts said"]. The euro rose from its recent 17-month low. It was last up 0.1% at $1.12315 . The Japanese yen weakened 0.03% against the greenback to 158.05 per dollar. European government bond yields edged higher, while US bond yields reversed earlier declines. Germany's 10-year yield rose 4.36 basis points to 3.453% . The yield on benchmark US 10-year notes rose 2.13 basis points to 5.108%. Even so, yields have eased this week as investors sought the safety of government debt amid concerns about AI-related companies' finances. G7 government bond markets were on course for their strongest weekly performance since late May. Brent crude futures rose 3.72% to settle at $109.86 a barrel and were headed for a second straight weekly gain amid concerns over Middle East supplies. Attacks around [USN:L1N46201B TEXT:"the Strait of Hormuz"] have surged in the past 10 days. Gold gained support from the weaker dollar, rising 0.25% to $4,159.69 an ounce.

item.title: Dollar heads for weekly loss as Fed hike bets fade, AI jitters linger
item.description: The dollar was lower on Friday and on track for its first weekly fall in more than a month against the euro and the yen, reflecting fading expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike and lingering concerns about an AI-driven equity selloff.
item.dc:creator: Laura Matthews
item.content:encoded: The dollar was lower on Friday and on track for its first weekly fall in more than a month against the euro and the yen, reflecting fading expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike and lingering concerns about an AI-driven equity selloff. [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"Hotter-than-expected consumer"] and producer price readings initially rattled markets this week, but comments from [USN:L1N4600EO TEXT:"Fed officials signaling"] no urgency to tighten policy further helped stabilize Treasury yields and eroded support for the dollar. AI stocks [USN:L6N460140 TEXT:"fell sharply"] this week and the [USN:L4N46112V TEXT:"stress spread"] to parts of the credit market as investors who have crowded into bets all along the supply chain [USN:L4N46112V TEXT:"worry"] data centre operators might not manage to be profitable in time to pay their debts. "What I found most interesting today and more broadly this week, is how closely the dollar has been tied to the AI trade," said Matt Weller, global head of market research at StoneX in Michigan. "Usually if we see a sell off in tech stocks you would expect the greenback to get a safe-haven bid. We are seeing an element of that into bonds, but the dollar is actually falling." The dollar index , which measures it against six major peers, fell 0.17% to 101.87 and was set for a 0.35% weekly drop. The pound and the Swiss franc led gains against the dollar this week, with the latter buoyed by safe-haven demand and expectations that even in a lower-rates environment Switzerland is unlikely to cut policy rates below the current zero level. Sterling rose 0.31% to $1.3314 and was up 0.63% on the week, while the dollar fell 0.25% against the Swiss franc to 0.8246, leaving it down 0.67% for the week. The franc has gained more than 1.4% in the last two sessions. Markets assign an 83% probability to the Fed keeping rates unchanged later this month, up from 49% a month earlier, the CME FedWatch Tool shows. At the IMF-World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok on Friday, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh [USN:S0N40K04F TEXT:"offered no clues"] about future rate decisions, saying he does not "prejudge meetings." "I don’t think there is enough support in (the) committee, particularly from the governors, for a rate hike in October. It still leaves December an unanswered question and there is a lot to happen between now and then," said John Velis, Americas macro strategist at BNY in New York. EURO AREA FISCAL RISKS STILL IN FOCUS Fiscal risks in France remained in the background after the [USN:L6N45N0H4 TEXT:"jump in the French debt risk premium"] in early October. The euro was last up 0.08% to $1.1227 after climbing 0.56% on Thursday in its biggest daily rise in two months, putting it on track for a 0.23% weekly gain. Investors expect US President Donald Trump to steer clear of any escalation in the Middle East or Ukraine, as a broader conflict could hurt his standing ahead of midterm elections by fuelling inflation. Against the yen the dollar slipped 0.08% to 158.11, leaving the Japanese currency on track for a 0.13% weekly rise after dropping for four consecutive weeks as the Iran conflict supported the greenback. Higher oil prices recently have been boosting the dollar while weighing on the currencies of energy-importing countries, such as those tied to the euro and yen. BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda on Friday reiterated the risks of [USN:L1N46207U TEXT:"underlying inflation overshooting"] the central bank's 2% target.

item.title: Oil touches $110 a barrel for first time since May on Middle East, Russia supply fears
item.description: Brent touched $110 a barrel for the first time since May on Friday on worries that escalating tensions in the Middle East could further tighten supplies, while investors assessed how much diesel Russia could supply to the global market.
item.dc:creator: Arathy Somasekhar
item.content:encoded: Brent touched $110 a barrel for the first time since May on Friday on worries that escalating tensions in the Middle East could further tighten supplies, while investors assessed how much diesel Russia could supply to the global market. Brent crude futures settled $3.94, or 3.7%, higher at $109.86, the highest since May 19, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures closed $3.44, or 3.5%, higher at $101.41, the highest since September 17. So far this week, Brent has risen 4.9% and WTI 10.4%. "WTI and Brent reversed earlier losses as escalation fears resurfaced amid rumours of attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure," research and consultancy Energy Aspects said in a note. " Israeli reports suggest Iran may be preparing a pre-emptive strike following unusual military movements detected by Western intelligence. Although unverified, these developments reinforce our view that persistent escalation risks will keep flat prices supported," Energy Aspects added. A Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched towards the Red Sea city of Yanbu. The port is critical for Saudi Arabia's efforts to bypass the Strait of Hormuz and keep oil flowing to international markets. Initial reports indicated no damage to Yanbu's infrastructure, consultants Rapidan Energy Group said. Supply concerns also increased as attacks around [USN:L1N4600JW TEXT:"the Strait of Hormuz"] surged over the past 10 days, with Iran saying it was stepping up strikes in response to the US blockade of its ports and tougher sanctions introduced last month. "Intensified Iranian attacks drove Gulf crude flows sharply lower," Kpler analysts said in a report on Thursday, adding that they expected a slower and more uneven recovery in Hormuz flows in the absence of a comprehensive political deal. RUSSIA REFINERY ATTACKS Ukraine struck a Russian oil refinery on Thursday after President Volodymyr Zelenskiy declared that Kyiv was abandoning a ceasefire covering energy sites announced by US President Donald Trump and criticized Trump's willingness to strike deals with Moscow. Russia's Ryazan oil refinery has suspended operations at a primary crude distillation unit following a drone attack in the region on Thursday, two industry sources told Reuters. "Conflict in the Middle East still keeps coming back and I think it's questionable how much diesel fuel Russia can actually deliver to the markets. Those two factors are just continuing to have traders be buyers," said Dennis Kissler, senior vice president of trading at BOK Financial. To boost supply, the International Energy Agency [USN:L1N4610MY TEXT:"agreed"] on Thursday to release more than 20 million barrels of fuel to the market. The United States also issued a request for proposal for an exchange of up to 17 million barrels of crude oil from the nation's Strategic Petroleum Reserve, the Department of Energy said on Friday. Washington previously agreed to loan 172 million barrels of oil from the SPR as part of a wider deal with about 30 countries in the International Energy Agency to release 400 million barrels from reserves around the world. Brent crude was little changed on Thursday, while WTI settled up more than 3% after news that the US was weighing plans to ease restrictions on the world’s "shadow fleet" of tankers and after a big [USN:L6N46115T TEXT:"US crude stock draw"] on hurricane production shut-ins.

item.title: OFRMO Summary
item.description: L'Iran exporte du GPL et du kérosène malgré le blocus américain, selon des données
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: L'Iran exporte du GPL et du kérosène malgré le blocus américain, selon des données DAMAS/LONDRES, 16 octobre (Reuters) - L’Iran a réussi à exporter quelques cargaisons de gaz de pétrole liquéfié (GPL) et de kérosène depuis juillet, malgré le blocus naval américain, selon des données de suivi du trafic maritime et des sources spécialisées dans la sécurité. Trump écarte la nouvelle porte-parole de la Maison Blanche WASHINGTON, 16 octobre - La porte-parole de la Maison Blanche, Katie Zacharia, a été "démise de ses fonctions", a déclaré vendredi un responsable de la Maison Blanche, après que le président Donald Trump a déclaré qu'il lui avait demandé d'envisager de démissionner. Trump affirme que ni lui ni Musk n'ont bridé Starlink en Ukraine WASHINGTON, 16 octobre (Reuters) - Le président américain Donald Trump a déclaré vendredi qu'il ne pensait pas que lui-même ou Elon Musk soient responsables du fait que l'armée ukrainienne n'ait plus accès aux capacités militaires de Starlink. Blue Origin vise plusieurs vols de New Glenn par semaine d’ici à 2030 WASHINGTON, 16 octobre (Reuters) - Blue Origin vise plusieurs vols par semaine de sa fusée New Glenn d’ici à la fin de la décennie, a déclaré vendredi un dirigeant de l’entreprise, alors que celle-ci investit des milliards de dollars dans les infrastructures nécessaires pour rivaliser avec SpaceX. Russie et États-Unis discutent de projets dans l'Arctique et dans le GNL, selon un émissaire russe 16 octobre (Reuters) - La Russie et les Etats-Unis discutent de projets dans l'Arctique et dans le gaz naturel liquéfié (GNL), a déclaré vendredi Kirill Dmitriev, l'envoyé spécial du président russe Vladimir Poutine chargé des investissements. USA: Une fusillade dans une école de l'Oregon fait quatre morts, le tireur abattu 15 octobre (Reuters) - Un adolescent de 16 ans a ouvert le feu jeudi dans une école primaire de Bend, dans l'Oregon, faisant quatre morts, dont trois enfants, avant d'être abattu par une personne qui l'avait poursuivi dans l'établissement, a annoncé la police. Attaques de drones russes sur plusieurs villes, dont Kharkiv, au moins trois morts 16 octobre (Reuters) - - Des attaques de drones russes ont fait au moins trois morts vendredi en Ukraine, deux à Kharkiv, la deuxième ville du pays, et un dans la région de Volyn (nord-ouest), ont rapporté les autorités. L'Ukraine dispose de réserves de gaz au plus haut niveau depuis 2020, selon le DG de Naftogaz KYIV, 16 octobre (Reuters) - Le directeur général par intérim de Naftogaz, la société publique ukrainienne du pétrole et du gaz, a dit à Reuters que l'entreprise avait constitué ses plus importantes réserves de gaz depuis six ans en prévision de l'hiver, malgré une recrudescence des frappes russes sur ses installations. Zelensky dénonce la "parodie" diplomatique de Moscou, fustige les expédients de Trump BRUXELLES/KYIV, 16 octobre (Reuters) - Volodimir Zelensky a durci le ton vendredi à l'égard de la Russie, accusée de feindre une "parodie" de processus de paix, et visé par ricochet Donald Trump auquel il reproche de "remplir les poches" de Vladimir Poutine pour poursuivre la guerre en Ukraine. La Chine est prête à coopérer avec l'UE pour remédier aux déséquilibres mondiaux PÉKIN, 16 octobre (Reuters) - La Chine est prête à engager un dialogue avec l'Union européenne (UE) pour améliorer la communication sur certains aspects de la gouvernance économique mondiale et de la coordination des politiques macroéconomiques, a déclaré vendredi le ministre chinois des Finances.
